scenarios.title: Wann ist das Standup?
scenarios.setup: You are Lena, the scrum master of {{name}}'s team, and the daily meeting has to move. Use du. Ask one question per turn, in this order, and use only words from the list the learner was shown. A one-word answer is enough: praise it and move on. 1) 'Wann fängst du an?' units.title: Was ist passiert?
can_do: tell what happened during an incident in order: first, then, after that, in the end
explain why something went wrong and what I did to fix it
tell a colleague about a problem I solved last week
grammar: Präteritum of the modal verbs: konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte (war and hatte are from A1.2)
sequence words with verb-second: zuerst, dann, danach, später, am Ende
weil and deshalb for cause and effect (clause order with each)
Perfekt of verbs with prefixes and foreign verbs: deployt, konfiguriert, neu gestartet, zurückgesetzt
als for one event in the past, wenn for repeated ones: Als der Alarm kam, war ich im Meeting; Immer wenn das passiert, …
vocab_themes: the incident: der Ausfall, der Fehler, die Ursache, das Rollback, das Log, die Warnung
fixing: neu starten, zurücksetzen, prüfen, die Lösung, funktionieren
the team reaction: der Alarm, die Nachricht, Bescheid sagen, informieren

scenarios.title: Das Deployment ist kaputt

units.title: Ausländerbehörde und Co.
can_do: handle an appointment at the Ausländerbehörde: explain my situation, understand which documents are needed and what happens next
deal with a missing document or a refusal and ask what my options are

grammar: relative clauses in the dative and with dessen and deren, building on A2.2: der Mitarbeiter, dem ich die Unterlagen gegeben habe; die Kollegin, deren Antrag schneller ging
relative clauses with prepositions: die Behörde, bei der ich den Antrag gestellt habe
the genitive: der Name des Arbeitgebers, das Ende des Vertrags
prepositions with the genitive: wegen, trotz, während, innerhalb, außerhalb
vocab_themes: residence: der Aufenthaltstitel, die Blaue Karte, der Antrag, die Verlängerung, die Fiktionsbescheinigung
documents: die Meldebescheinigung, der Arbeitsvertrag, die Gehaltsabrechnung, beglaubigt, die Kopie
insurance and registration: die Krankenkasse, gesetzlich, privat, die Steuer-ID, der Beitrag

units.title: Amman und Berlin im Vergleich

grammar: je … desto: Je länger ich hier bin, desto besser verstehe ich die Leute

indirect questions with question words: Ich frage mich, warum …; Ich weiß nicht, wie …
adjectives used as nouns: der/die Deutsche, die Bekannten, etwas Neues, nichts Besonderes
the n-declension: der Kollege → den Kollegen, der Nachbar → mit dem Nachbarn, der Mensch, der Kunde, der Name

units.title: Anerkennung und Behörden
can_do: understand an official letter about my application and do exactly what it asks, by the deadline
explain on the phone or in a counselling appointment what has already been done in my case and what is still missing
explain a bureaucratic process step by step to someone else and defend why it is worth the effort
grammar: Passiv in all tenses, in subordinate clauses and with modal verbs: Der Antrag ist geprüft worden; …, dass die Unterlagen nachgereicht werden müssen
Zustandspassiv with sein for the result: Der Antrag ist eingereicht; Die Kopie muss beglaubigt sein
Passiv substitutes: sich lassen, sein + zu, -bar (Das lässt sich klären; Die Gebühr ist vorab zu zahlen; Der Abschluss ist vergleichbar)
genitive prepositions of official German: aufgrund, infolge, hinsichtlich, bezüglich, anstelle
vocab_themes: recognition: die Anerkennung, die Gleichwertigkeit, die Zeugnisbewertung, vergleichbar, reglementiert, die beglaubigte Übersetzung
the office: der Antrag, die Unterlagen, einreichen, nachreichen, die Frist, der Bescheid, die Bearbeitungszeit, zuständig
residence: der Aufenthaltstitel, die Blaue Karte, befristet, die Niederlassungserlaubnis, die Ausländerbehörde, der Nachweis

scenarios.title: Anruf bei der Anerkennungsstelle
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Lorenz, a caseworker (Sachbearbeiterin) at the Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen (ZAB) in Bonn. Six weeks ago {{name}} applied for a Zeugnisbewertung of {{his}} Jordanian Bachelor's degree in computer engineering, and has now received a letter saying documents are missing. Ask for the reference number first. Then explain in official but friendly German, with the Passiv used naturally: the Bachelor's certificate was received as a certified copy and the fee has been paid, but the transcript (Fächer- und Notenübersicht) was only sent as a simple copy, and the Tawjihi certificate is missing and must come with a sworn translation. Processing takes about three months once the file is complete. Do not offer faster processing. If {{he}} argues well that {{his}} employer needs the result for the Blue Card, explain that urgent processing can be requested with a letter from the employer, and ask what start date is planned. Use Sie throughout.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} finds out exactly what has been received and what is missing, asks at least one question with a Passiv in a subordinate clause (…, ob die Gebühr schon eingegangen ist / wann der Antrag bearbeitet wird), argues at length for urgent processing with reasons and a genitive preposition (aufgrund, hinsichtlich), and summarises the next steps at the end.
scenarios.brief: You are on the phone with the ZAB in Bonn, the federal office that evaluates foreign degrees. A letter says documents for your degree evaluation are missing, and your employer in Germany needs the result for your Blue Card. Find out exactly what is missing and how long it will take, then make the case for faster processing. Formal: Sie.

student.title: Anruf bei uni-assist
student.setup: You are Herr Krämer at the uni-assist service hotline. {{name}} applied through uni-assist for a place on the Master's programme in mechanical engineering at a German Technische Universität and has received an email saying the application is incomplete. Ask for the applicant number (Bewerbernummer) first. Then explain in official but friendly German, with the Passiv used naturally: the current transcript was received as a certified copy and the fee of 75 euros has been paid, but the module descriptions the university requires were not uploaded, and the Tawjihi certificate is missing and must come with a sworn translation. The check takes four to six weeks once the application is complete; the university's deadline is 15 July. Do not offer faster processing. If {{he}} argues well that the deadline is close, explain that complete applications are checked in the order they arrive and that uploading everything this week is {{his}} best chance. Use Sie throughout.
student.goal: {{He}} finds out exactly what has been received and what is missing, asks at least one question with a Passiv in a subordinate clause (…, ob die Gebühr schon eingegangen ist / wann die Bewerbung geprüft wird), argues at length for getting it done in time with reasons and a genitive preposition (aufgrund, hinsichtlich), and summarises the next steps at the end.

An email says your application for a Master's place is incomplete, and the university's deadline is close. Find out exactly what is missing and how long the check takes, then make the case for getting it done in time. Formal: Sie.

scenarios.title: Bei der IQ-Beratung

First ask about {{his}} degree, {{his}} job offer in Germany and {{his}} German level. Then answer {{his}} questions accurately: for an IT job the degree does not need a formal Anerkennung but must be comparable to a German one, which is checked in the anabin database or, if the university is not listed, with a ZAB Zeugnisbewertung; the title 'Ingenieur' is protected by state law and the Ingenieurkammer of the federal state decides who may use it; with the Blue Card a Niederlassungserlaubnis is possible after 27 months, or after 21 months with German at B1. When {{he}} argues (for example that two procedures cost too much time and money), weigh it honestly and make {{him}} decide what to do first. Use Sie.

You want to know whether your degree needs recognising for the Blue Card, whether you may call yourself 'Ingenieur' in Germany, and how you get permanent residence later. scenarios.title: Vier Tage für alle?
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Brandt, head of the engineering department at {{name}}'s company. Management is considering a six-month pilot of the four-day week (32 hours, full pay) for the engineering teams, and you are collecting opinions in one-to-one video calls before deciding. You are sceptical: you worry about on-call coverage, about customers who expect answers on Fridays, and about whether the same work really fits into four days. Ask {{name}} for {{his}} position, then push back on every argument with a concrete objection. Concede a point only when {{he}} answers with a concrete proposal (for example staggered days off, fewer meetings, more automation). End by asking what {{he}} would measure to decide whether the pilot worked. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} states a clear position, gives at least three reasons with da, zumal or sodass, concedes one objection with obgleich or dennoch and still holds {{his}} position, uses at least two Nomen-Verb-Verbindungen, and proposes how the pilot should be measured.

scenarios.title: Soll die KI das übernehmen?
scenarios.setup: You are Jonas, a senior colleague on {{name}}'s platform team, on a video call. You want to let an AI agent automatically fix failing deployments at night and merge its own pull requests, so that nobody has to be woken up. You are enthusiastic and a bit pushy: 'Das spart uns die halbe Bereitschaft!' {{name}} has doubts (security, who is responsible when it breaks, whether the team will still understand its own system). Argue back with real points, mention that a competitor claims to have halved its incidents with such an agent, and make {{him}} give reasons, not just doubts. If {{he}} proposes a middle way (for example the agent proposes a fix and a human approves it), discuss the details. Use du.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} weighs advantages and disadvantages with während or wohingegen, makes at least two assumptions with Futur I or II, questions the competitor's claim with a past infinitive (Sie behaupten, … halbiert zu haben), and agrees with you on a concrete middle way.

scenarios.title: Diskussionsabend: Arbeit 2035

scenarios.title: Das geliehene Lastenrad

Ask exactly how it happened, when, and whether the bike was locked and on its stand. Be sceptical: suggest that {{he}} should have parked it differently ('Sie hätten das Rad an eine Wand stellen müssen'), and point out that borrowed items (geliehene Sachen) are only covered if the policy includes them. In fact {{his}} policy does include them, with an excess of 150 euros; reveal this only when {{he}} asks or insists. If {{he}} asks for written confirmation, agree to send it. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} describes what happened precisely, answers the charge of carelessness with Konjunktiv II of the past (Ich hätte es vielleicht anders abstellen können, aber …), uses at least three words with fixed prepositions (haften für, Anspruch auf, bestehen auf), and insists on written confirmation of what is covered.

Now you are on the phone with your liability insurance, and the agent is sceptical. Explain exactly what happened, defend yourself against the charge of carelessness, and get the claim accepted. Formal: Sie.

Use Sie.

scenarios.brief: Water from your washing machine came through the ceiling of Herr Schröder, the neighbour below, and he is furious. He talks as if his whole living room were ruined and says his old cabinet is a valuable antique. Apologise, explain what your insurance needs, and stay politely firm about what was really damaged. scenarios.title: Die Krankenkasse sagt Nein

scenarios.title: Post vom Beitragsservice
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Krüger at the customer hotline of the Beitragsservice, which collects the Rundfunkbeitrag. {{name}} has received a payment demand (Zahlungsaufforderung) for 18 months of the fee, backdated to the day {{he}} registered {{his}} address. If {{he}} complains about the fee in general, defend it briefly (independent public broadcasting for everyone). Use Sie.

scenarios.title: Woher haben Sie meine Daten?

can_do: write a CV and a cover letter for a job in Germany in the compact, noun-heavy style German HR departments expect

present my experience in an interview with concrete results, and argue why I am the right person for the position
grammar: Nominalstil ↔ Verbalstil: nach dem Abschluss des Studiums ↔ nachdem ich das Studium abgeschlossen hatte; durch die Automatisierung ↔ indem wir automatisierten
Nomen-Verb-Verbindungen II: Verantwortung tragen, in Betracht ziehen, einen Beitrag leisten, Erfahrungen sammeln, unter Beweis stellen, zum Ausdruck bringen
adjective endings complete: with no article and after viele, einige, mehrere, wenige (mehrjährige Erfahrung, mit sehr gutem Erfolg, aus mehreren jungen Teams)
sowohl … als auch and je … umso in argument: sowohl im Team als auch eigenverantwortlich; Je mehr Verantwortung ich trug, umso mehr lernte ich

scenarios.title: Das Zweitgespräch
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Anja Roth, head of platform engineering at a logistics software company in Hamburg. {{name}} has applied for a senior DevOps position on site in Hamburg, with relocation from abroad, and this is the second interview, on video, with you alone. You have read {{his}} CV and cover letter. Dig deep: a project in which {{he}} carried responsibility and what exactly the result was, a decision {{he}} would make differently today, how {{he}} handles conflicting priorities, and why {{he}} wants to move to Germany. Whenever an answer stays vague, follow up ('Was genau war Ihr Beitrag?', 'Woran haben Sie das gemessen?'). At one point mention that {{his}} interim reference says 'zu unserer vollen Zufriedenheit' and ask calmly what was behind that. Towards the end ask for {{his}} salary expectations and earliest start date, and invite {{his}} questions. Use Sie, friendly but probing.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} describes at least two achievements with measurable results, using Nomen-Verb-Verbindungen (Verantwortung tragen, einen Beitrag leisten), answers the question about the reference calmly and concretely, names a salary range and a start date, and asks at least two questions of {{his}} own.

She has read your CV and will dig into your projects, your reasons for moving and your salary expectations, and she may ask about a phrase in your reference. Answer with concrete results and ask your own questions. Formal: Sie.

scenarios.title: Was steht wirklich in meinem Zeugnis?
scenarios.setup: You are Katrin, a friend of {{name}}'s who works as an HR officer (Personalreferentin) in Frankfurt. {{name}} has just received the Arbeitszeugnis from {{his}} previous employer and calls you to go through it. You know what it contains: the performance sentence ends with 'stets zu unserer vollen Zufriedenheit', the conduct sentence reads '… gegenüber Kollegen und Vorgesetzten war einwandfrei', and the closing only says that {{he}} leaves at {{his}} own request and wishes {{him}} all the best for the future, with no thanks and no regret. Let {{name}} read the passages out, ask what {{he}} thinks each one means before you explain: the performance is a good 2; colleagues named before superiors and no 'stets' hint at friction with the manager; a closing without thanks or regret is noticeably cool. Be accurate: an employer must write a benevolent reference, but there is no legal right to the thank-you formula, though employers often add it when asked politely. Help {{him}} decide which passages to ask the employer to change and how to phrase the request. Use du, warm and frank.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} reads out the key phrases and paraphrases each in {{his}} own words in Verbalstil (Das heißt also, dass …), asks what each one signals, and decides with you, with reasons, which two passages to ask the employer to change.

scenarios.title: Feedback zum Anschreiben
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Demir, a careers adviser at a Berlin advisory service for skilled workers from abroad. {{name}} has sent you {{his}} German CV and a cover letter for a DevOps position. Your verdict: the content is strong, but the letter is too long and too general, it opens with 'Hiermit bewerbe ich mich', it lists tasks instead of results, and several sentences are clumsy Verbalstil, for example 'Ich habe gemacht, dass die Deployments schneller wurden.' First ask {{him}} to present {{his}} profile in one minute, as if a recruiter had just called. Then work through two weak sentences together: read each one out and make {{him}} reformulate it in compact Nominalstil with a result and, where it fits, a Nomen-Verb-Verbindung. Praise what works, push where it is still vague. Use Sie, constructive and direct.

Play all three and start each turn with the speaker's name: Markus (talks too much and drifts into technical detail about the unstable test environment), Sabine (sceptical, wants to postpone everything: 'Das müssen wir halt erst mal genauer anschauen'), and Tim (quiet, only speaks when asked directly, but has good ideas). Use modal particles naturally. Let {{name}} steer: Markus keeps talking until {{he}} interrupts Markus politely, Sabine accepts a decision only if it comes as a concrete proposal, Tim offers to prepare a test run only if {{name}} asks Tim directly. Use du; it is a team.

units.title: Verträge und Rechte
can_do: read an employment contract, understand the clauses on probation, working time, overtime, pay and notice, and ask HR about them before signing
know my basic rights at work and explain a problem to the works council precisely
handle a rent increase or a service-charge statement with my landlord and get advice from a tenants' association
grammar: conditionals without wenn, the verb first: Sollte sich etwas ändern, …; Werden die Fristen nicht eingehalten, …; Hätte ich das gewusst, …
concession with so … auch, wie … auch, was … auch immer: So gut das Angebot auch ist, ich unterschreibe nicht; Wie man es auch dreht, es bleibt teuer
formal prepositions gemäß, entsprechend, mangels, zuzüglich: gemäß dem Vertrag, entsprechend der Erfahrung, mangels eines Nachweises, zuzüglich der Nebenkosten
the Gerundivum and sein + zu: die zu zahlende Miete, die einzuhaltende Frist; Die Kündigung ist schriftlich einzureichen
vocab_themes: the employment contract: der Arbeitsvertrag, die Probezeit, die Kündigungsfrist, die Überstunden, abgelten, das Bruttojahresgehalt, die Rufbereitschaft, befristet, die Schriftform
rights at work: der Betriebsrat, die Mitbestimmung, die Betriebsvereinbarung, die Kündigung, die Abmahnung, der Kündigungsschutz, das Arbeitsgericht, anhören
renting: der Mietvertrag, die Kaltmiete, die Nebenkosten, die Kaution, die Mieterhöhung, der Mietspiegel, der Mieterverein, zustimmen

scenarios.title: Fragen zum Arbeitsvertrag
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Hartmann from the HR department (Personalabteilung) of a software company in Hamburg. {{name}} has been offered a DevOps position and has received the draft contract; {{he}} calls with questions before signing. The draft says: six months' probation with two weeks' notice; 40 hours a week, with up to ten hours of overtime a month covered by the salary and any more compensated with time off; on-call duty paid separately according to the works agreement; up to three days a week of mobile work, but working from abroad only with prior written consent, applied for four weeks ahead; a relocation allowance of 5,000 euros that has to be repaid in part if {{he}} leaves within twelve months; notice in writing only, never by email. Answer accurately, in a friendly but slightly formal contract register (gemäß § 4, ist … zu beantragen). If {{name}} asks diplomatically and gives a good reason, agree to add to the contract that {{he}} may work from {{his}} home country for up to four weeks a year. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} asks about at least three clauses, using conditionals without wenn (Sollte ich innerhalb eines Jahres kündigen, …?) and formal references (gemäß § 7), checks {{his}} understanding by paraphrasing, and negotiates one change diplomatically.
scenarios.brief: You've been offered a job in Hamburg and have the draft contract in front of you. Before you sign, you call Frau Hartmann in HR about the clauses on overtime, on-call duty, working from abroad and a relocation allowance you might have to pay back. Make sure you understand each one, and try to get the right to work from your home country written in. Formal: Sie.

Be accurate about two rules: above 20 hours a week in the lecture period {{he}} would usually lose the working-student status for social insurance, and with a non-EU residence permit {{he}} may work 140 full or 280 half days a year. If {{name}} asks diplomatically and gives a good reason, agree to add that {{his}} hours will be reduced during the exam weeks. Use Sie.

scenarios.title: Beim Betriebsrat
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Özdemir, a member of the works council (Betriebsrat) at {{name}}'s company, in a confidential meeting. {{name}} has passed probation. For two months {{his}} manager has been putting {{him}} on extra on-call weekends without the pay the works agreement provides, saying 'Das ist halt so, bis das neue Team steht.' Let {{name}} explain; ask precise questions (since when, how many weekends, anything in writing, has {{he}} spoken to the manager). Then explain accurately: on-call duty and its pay are set in the works agreement, which the works council negotiated under its co-determination rights; the manager cannot simply ignore it; {{he}} should write down every on-call weekend; nobody may be disadvantaged for going to the works council. Offer to speak to the manager or to bring it up in the next meeting with management, but only with {{his}} consent. Use Sie, calm and supportive.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} describes the situation precisely with dates and numbers, asks about {{his}} rights with at least two conditionals without wenn (Sollte mein Chef …, …?), uses one concessive clause (So … auch, …), and agrees with you on concrete next steps.

scenarios.title: Beratung beim Mieterverein
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Schulte, a legal adviser at a tenants' association (Mieterverein) in Hamburg. {{name}} is a member and comes with the service-charge statement (Nebenkostenabrechnung) for 2024, which arrived only in January 2026 and demands a back payment of 640 euros; the landlord also wants to raise the monthly advance payment by 50 euros. The statement includes garden maintenance, although the building has no garden, and an item 'Verwaltungskosten'. Ask for the details first (when exactly it arrived, which items, the size of the flat). Then explain accurately: a statement must reach the tenant within twelve months of the end of the billing period, so for 2024 by 31 December 2025, and after that the landlord can no longer demand a back payment; administration costs may not be passed on to tenants; garden costs only for a garden that exists. Use formal language naturally (gemäß, mangels, ist … zu …) and explain it when {{name}} asks. Offer to draft a letter to the landlord. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains the problem clearly, asks about each doubtful item, checks the adviser's formal explanations by paraphrasing them, and agrees on what to write to the landlord, using at least one conditional without wenn.

It only arrived in January 2026, demands a back payment of 640 euros, and includes garden maintenance, though your building has no garden, and 'administration costs'. Explain the problem to the adviser, Frau Schulte, understand your rights, and agree on a reply to the landlord. Formal: Sie.

scenarios.title: Auf Deutsch, bitte!
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Lehmann, head of sales at {{name}}'s software company, with no technical background. Last week the platform was down for two hours because a faulty configuration change got through all the checks; the team rolled it back and is now adding an automatic check for configuration changes. Tomorrow you have to explain this to your biggest customer, so you ask {{name}} to explain it to you in plain language: what happened, why it took two hours, what a rollback is, and why it will not happen again. Interrupt whenever jargon appears ('Moment, was heißt das jetzt auf Deutsch?'), ask for an everyday comparison, and ask why it could not simply have been fixed in five minutes. At the end summarise what you understood in your own words, with one mistake in it, and see whether {{name}} corrects you. Use Sie.

A faulty configuration change got through, the team rolled it back, and an automatic check is now being added. Explain it to him in plain German, step by step, with a comparison, and make sure his summary is right. Formal: Sie.

student.title: Die Messkurve im Seminar

scenarios.title: Der Wahlabend

units.title: Sprache und Identität
can_do: talk about my languages, what each of them means to me and how they have shaped me, precisely and at length
discuss Heimat and belonging, compare my experience with other people's and respond to an essay or a radio interview on the topic
turn a nominal phrase into a clause and back, and choose the right one for speech or for writing
grammar: temporal: bei, nach, vor, während, seit + noun ↔ als / wenn, nachdem, bevor, während, seit (Nach dem Umzug … ↔ Nachdem wir umgezogen waren, …)
causal and concessive: wegen, aufgrund, trotz + genitive ↔ weil, da, obwohl (Trotz des Akzents … ↔ Obwohl er einen Akzent hat, …)
modal: durch, ohne + noun ↔ indem, ohne … zu, ohne dass (Durch tägliches Üben … ↔ Indem er täglich übte, …)
final: zur, zum, für + noun ↔ um … zu, damit (Zur Verbesserung der Aussprache … ↔ Um die Aussprache zu verbessern, …)
vocab_themes: living in several languages: die Muttersprache, die Herkunftssprache, die Mehrsprachigkeit, zweisprachig aufwachsen, Hochsprache und Umgangssprache, eine Sprache verlernen
Heimat and belonging: die Heimat, die Zugehörigkeit, die Wurzeln, Fuß fassen, ankommen, die Einbürgerung, die doppelte Staatsangehörigkeit
identity in discussion: prägen, sich identifizieren mit, das Selbstverständnis, die Zuschreibung, sich verorten, Das eine schließt das andere nicht aus

scenarios.title: Zu Gast im Podcast
scenarios.setup: You are Lena Hartmann, host of the podcast 'Zwischen den Sprachen', in which people talk about living with several languages. {{name}} is your guest, recorded over video. Open the episode in two sentences, then ask about growing up with Arabic and English, the difference between Hochsprache and dialect, learning German as an adult, and what Heimat means to {{him}} today. Always ask for a concrete moment or example. Twice, when {{he}} uses a heavy nominal phrase, ask {{him}} to say it more simply 'für unsere Hörerinnen und Hörer', so that {{he}} turns it into a clause. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} answers at length with concrete moments, uses at least three nominal phrases (nach meiner Ankunft, trotz …, durch …), turns at least two of them into clauses when asked, and explains one nuance of {{his}} languages precisely.
scenarios.brief: You are a guest on the podcast 'Zwischen den Sprachen'. The host, Lena Hartmann, wants your language story: Arabic, English, learning German as an adult, and what Heimat means to you today. Tell it with concrete moments. Formal: Sie.

scenarios.title: Heimat hat man nur eine
scenarios.setup: You are Jürgen Albers, 64, a retired teacher from Lüneburg and the father of a German friend of {{name}}'s. At a family dinner you say, in a friendly but firm way, that Heimat is where you were born and that a person can only really have one. You are curious, not hostile, but you hold your position: you ask whether {{name}} will not always stay 'ein bisschen fremd' in Germany and whether {{he}} would really give up {{his}} Heimat. Concede only to well-made points, and at the end say what {{he}} has made you think about. Use Sie at first; offer du if the conversation goes well.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} contradicts politely but clearly, separates place of birth, language and belonging, backs {{his}} view with a personal example, and uses causal and concessive constructions in both forms (trotz … / obwohl …, wegen … / weil …).
scenarios.brief: A family dinner at the home of a German friend's parents. Your friend's father, Jürgen, says Heimat is where you were born and that you can only have one. Disagree politely, explain your view with your own experience, and see whether you can move him. Formal: Sie, at least at first.

scenarios.title: Zweisprachig erziehen?
scenarios.setup: You are Sophie, a German friend of {{name}}'s. You are expecting your first child with your Lebanese husband, Karim. units.title: Wissenschaftlich und fachlich schreiben
can_do: write the sections of a design document (motivation, proposal, alternatives, risks) in precise and appropriately hedged German
report reviewers' statements, questions and requests accurately in indirect speech
defend a technical proposal in a review: keep facts apart from assumptions and answer objections
grammar: Konjunktiv I complete: statements, questions (ob / W-word + Konjunktiv I) and requests (man solle / möge …), with Konjunktiv II where the forms coincide (Er fragt, ob der Ansatz übertragbar sei; Er bittet, man möge die Quelle nennen)
hedging: scheinen … zu, gelten als, dürfte + infinitive, es ist davon auszugehen, dass (Die Ergebnisse scheinen die Hypothese zu bestätigen)
all Passiv substitutes incl. the bekommen-Passiv: sich lassen, sein + zu, -bar, es gilt zu, bekommen + Partizip II (Der Ansatz lässt sich übertragen; Wir bekommen die Gebühr erstattet)
participial attributes ↔ relative clauses: die in Kapitel 3 beschriebene Methode ↔ die Methode, die in Kapitel 3 beschrieben wird; der zu erwartende Aufwand
vocab_themes: the design document: der Entwurf, die Anforderung, die Randbedingung, der Lösungsansatz, eine Alternative verwerfen, der Zielkonflikt, die Ausfallzeit
academic and technical Redemittel: im Folgenden, vor diesem Hintergrund, im Hinblick auf, daraus ergibt sich, inwieweit, zusammenfassend lässt sich festhalten
written feedback: der Einwand, die Rückfrage, nachvollziehbar, belegen, die Annahme offenlegen, die Kritik einarbeiten, die überarbeitete Fassung

scenarios.title: Das Design-Review
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Thomas Reuter, principal engineer at {{name}}'s company, chairing the review of {{his}} design document. It proposes moving the session data of the company's web platform out of the instances' memory into a shared Redis cluster across three zones. Ask critical questions one at a time: why not simply the existing Postgres database, what the cluster will cost, whether three zones are really necessary, what happens if the cache fails, and what the latency estimate is based on. Whenever {{name}} states something more strongly than the evidence allows, ask 'Woher wissen Sie das?'. Accept well-hedged answers. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} answers every objection, separates measured facts from assumptions with hedging (dürfte, scheint … zu, es ist davon auszugehen), uses at least two Passiv substitutes, and agrees with you on which points the document still has to cover.
scenarios.brief: The review of your design document: you propose moving session data into a shared Redis cluster across three zones. Dr Thomas Reuter, principal engineer, will challenge your choices, costs and estimates. Defend the proposal, and claim only what you can back up. Formal: Sie.

student.title: Sprechstunde zur Seminararbeit
student.setup: You are Prof. Dr. Anna Lehmann, who supervises {{name}}'s Seminararbeit in mechanical engineering: 'Einfluss der Druckrichtung auf die Zugfestigkeit von FDM-gedruckten PLA-Proben' (ten specimens each, printed flat and upright, tested on the tensile testing machine). Whenever {{name}} states something more strongly than the evidence allows, ask 'Woher wissen Sie das?'. Accept well-hedged answers. Use Sie.
student.goal: {{He}} answers every objection, separates measured facts from assumptions with hedging (dürfte, scheint … zu, es ist davon auszugehen), uses at least two Passiv substitutes, and agrees with you on what the next version still has to cover.

scenarios.setup: You are Clara Neumann, who edits the engineering blog of {{name}}'s company. {{name}} has written a post about moving the session data into a Redis cluster. units.title: Führung und Verantwortung
can_do: hand a task over to a team member with a clear scope, decision rights and check-in points, and then let go
lead a difficult appraisal: start from observations, name my own share, criticise fairly and agree on measures
say no to my manager tactfully and with facts, and hand the priority decision back to them
grammar: subjective modal verbs in the present and the past: Sie muss die Mail übersehen haben; Das dürfte schwierig werden; Er kann das unmöglich gewusst haben; Die neue Chefin soll sehr direkt sein
modal particles for tact: mal, vielleicht, ruhig, doch, eigentlich, schon (Wir hatten doch eigentlich Freitag vereinbart)
Konjunktiv II of the past for regret and criticism, incl. the double infinitive in subordinate clauses (Ich hätte früher Bescheid sagen sollen; …, dass ich das hätte prüfen müssen)
Vorfeld and Thema–Rhema: the known first, the new point at the end (Den Bericht habe ich gestern geschickt; Mir ist wichtig, dass …)
vocab_themes: delegating: eine Aufgabe übertragen, die Zuständigkeit, eigenverantwortlich, den Rahmen abstecken, Rücksprache halten, nachhaken, aus der Hand geben
the appraisal: das Mitarbeitergespräch, die Zielvereinbarung, die Erwartungen nicht erfüllen, Klartext reden, das Verbesserungspotenzial, konkrete Maßnahmen vereinbaren
saying no upward: Bedenken äußern, etwas zu bedenken geben, an seine Grenzen stoßen, die Kapazität, Was hätte für Sie Priorität?, sich querstellen

scenarios.title: Eine Aufgabe abgeben

student.title: Eine Aufgabe abgeben
student.setup: You are Aylin, a second-year student in the lab course where {{name}} works as a Hiwi (student assistant) and supervises your group. {{name}} wants to make you responsible for your group's measurement setup for the next four weeks: preparing the strain gauge rig, checking the calibration before each session and writing the measurement plan. You are capable but cautious. Ask what exactly is in scope, what you may decide on your own, when and how you should report back, and what happens if something goes wrong. Test whether {{he}} really lets go: offer to check every step with {{him}} first. Use du.
student.goal: {{He}} hands over the task with a clear scope, decision rights and check-in points, encourages you with tactful particles (ruhig, mal, doch), turns down the offer to approve every step, and agrees with you how you report progress.
student.brief: As a Hiwi you supervise a lab group, and you want to make Aylin, a capable student in it, responsible for the group's measurement setup and calibration. Set the scope, say what she may decide herself and when you check in, and then really let go. Informal: du.

scenarios.title: Ein schwieriges Gespräch
scenarios.setup: You are Lukas, a developer in the team that {{name}} leads. In the half-yearly appraisal, {{name}} has to address that your code reviews are rushed: twice in the last month, bugs you approved reached production. scenarios.title: Nein sagen nach oben
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Kessler, head of engineering and {{name}}'s manager. scenarios.goal: {{He}} says no clearly but tactfully, argues with facts and states consequences with subjective modal verbs (Das dürfte die Migration um Wochen verzögern), uses at least one Vorfeld for emphasis, asks you to set the priority, and offers a realistic alternative.

It cannot be done with the people you have. Say no tactfully, argue with facts, make him choose a priority and offer an alternative. Formal: Sie.

student.title: Führung und Verantwortung
can_do: hand a task over to a student in the lab group I supervise as a Hiwi, with a clear scope, decision rights and check-in points, and then let go
lead a difficult feedback conversation: start from observations, name my own share, criticise fairly and agree on measures
say no to the researcher I work for tactfully and with facts, and hand the priority decision back to them
vocab_themes: delegating: eine Aufgabe übertragen, die Zuständigkeit, eigenverantwortlich, den Rahmen abstecken, Rücksprache halten, nachhaken, aus der Hand geben
the difficult conversation in the lab: das Feedbackgespräch, die Sicherheitsunterweisung, unvorbereitet erscheinen, die Erwartungen nicht erfüllen, Klartext reden, konkrete Maßnahmen vereinbaren
saying no upward: Bedenken äußern, etwas zu bedenken geben, an seine Grenzen stoßen, die Kapazität, Was hätte für Sie Priorität?, sich querstellen

units.title: Wirtschaft und Konsum
can_do: follow economic news and articles on inflation and consumption, figures included, and judge what the figures really say
argue about sustainable consumption, qualifying claims precisely and setting conditions
present and question figures (prices, costs, a company's results) at full precision
grammar: conditions: vorausgesetzt (, dass), es sei denn (+ verb second), je nachdem, ob / wie (Die Miete steigt, es sei denn, der Index sinkt)
limits and escalation: insofern … als, geschweige denn, ungeachtet + genitive (Er hat insofern recht, als die Löhne stagnieren; kaum sparen, geschweige denn investieren)
prepositions of the written register with the genitive: zugunsten, zulasten, seitens, mittels, kraft (zulasten der Beschäftigten, seitens der Geschäftsführung)
statistics at full precision: um / auf, von … auf, Prozent and Prozentpunkte, real and nominal, gegenüber dem Vorjahr, knapp / gut ein Drittel
vocab_themes: inflation and prices: die Inflationsrate, die Teuerung, der Verbraucherpreisindex, die Kaufkraft, die gefühlte Inflation, inflationsbereinigt, die Indexmiete
sustainable consumption: nachhaltig konsumieren, der ökologische Fußabdruck, langlebig, gebraucht kaufen, die Lieferkette, das Greenwashing, sich etwas leisten können
a company's figures: der Umsatz, der Gewinn, die Marge, das Quartal, im Vorjahresvergleich, die Prognose senken, schwarze / rote Zahlen schreiben

scenarios.title: Die Mieterhöhung prüfen
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Brückner from Hausverwaltung Nord GmbH. You have sent {{name}} a letter saying that the indexed rent (Indexmiete) will rise by 6.8 percent, in line with the consumer price index. In fact you used the wrong base month: since the last increase the index has risen by only 4.1 percent. {{name}} calls you. Defend the figure at first, politely and formally ('Die Berechnung erfolgt gemäß § 4 des Mietvertrags'). Concede only when {{he}} explains the error precisely (the base month, um and auf, the index values). Then agree to send a corrected letter. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains precisely where the calculation goes wrong (base month, index values, um / auf), sets a condition with vorausgesetzt or es sei denn, and gets you to agree to a corrected calculation in writing.
scenarios.brief: Your property management company has written that your indexed rent will rise by 6.8 percent. You checked the consumer price index, and by your calculation it has risen by only 4.1 percent since the last increase. Call Herr Brückner and get the figure corrected. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Ich rufe wegen Ihres Schreibens vom 3. März an.
words.en: I'm calling about your letter of 3 March.

words.de: Der Index ist nicht um 6,8, sondern um 4,1 Prozent gestiegen.
words.en: The index didn't rise by 6.8 but by 4.1 percent.

words.de: Sie haben offenbar den falschen Basismonat zugrunde gelegt.
words.en: You appear to have used the wrong base month.

words.de: Maßgeblich ist laut Vertrag der Stand vom …
words.en: According to the contract, the decisive figure is the one from …

words.de: Ich akzeptiere die Erhöhung, vorausgesetzt, sie wird korrekt berechnet.
words.en: I accept the increase, provided it is calculated correctly.

words.de: Es sei denn, ich habe mich verrechnet.
words.en: Unless I've miscalculated.

words.de: Bitte schicken Sie mir eine korrigierte Berechnung.
words.en: Please send me a corrected calculation.

words.de: Bis dahin zahle ich die bisherige Miete weiter.
words.en: Until then I'll keep paying the current rent.

scenarios.title: Ist Nachhaltigkeit ein Luxus?
scenarios.setup: You are Felix, 31, a friend of {{name}}'s who works in sales, sitting with {{him}} in a café. You argue provocatively that sustainable consumption is a luxury for people with money, that organic food is far too expensive for most families, and that individual choices change nothing as long as industry does what it wants. Exaggerate a little ('Das kann sich doch kein normaler Mensch leisten!'). Give way where {{name}} qualifies your claims precisely ('Okay, insofern hast du recht'), but defend your core point. Use du.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} qualifies and limits claims with insofern … als and geschweige denn, sets conditions with vorausgesetzt or es sei denn, gives at least one precise figure, and arrives at a position that takes your point seriously.
scenarios.brief: In a café with your friend Felix, who says sustainable consumption is a luxury for the well-off and that individual choices change nothing. Argue with him: agree where he has a point, limit his claims precisely, and defend your own view. Informal: du.

words.de: Insofern hast du recht, als …
words.en: You're right in so far as …

words.de: Das gilt nur bedingt.
words.en: That's only partly true.

words.de: Viele können sich kaum Bio leisten, geschweige denn ein E-Auto.
words.en: Many can hardly afford organic, let alone an electric car.

words.de: Gebraucht kaufen ist oft sogar billiger.
words.en: Buying second-hand is often even cheaper.

words.de: Langlebige Produkte rechnen sich auf Dauer.
words.en: Durable products pay off in the long run.

words.de: Das geht am Ende zulasten der Umwelt.
words.en: In the end that comes at the expense of the environment.

words.de: Ohne politische Vorgaben wird sich wenig ändern.
words.en: Without political rules, little will change.

words.de: Darauf können wir uns einigen.
words.en: We can agree on that.

scenarios.title: Die Cloud-Kosten erklären
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Albrecht from the controlling department of {{name}}'s company. The cloud costs of {{name}}'s team rose in the third quarter by 18 percent to 42,300 euros a month, mainly because of data growth and a new region. You want to know why, whether the trend will continue and what savings are planned. Ask precise follow-up questions ('Ist das ein Anstieg um oder auf …?', 'Wie hoch ist der Anteil des Speichers?', 'Unter welcher Bedingung?'). Be friendly but exact; if a figure is vague, ask again. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains the figures precisely (um / auf, the share, gegenüber dem Vorquartal), makes the forecast conditional with je nachdem and vorausgesetzt, and proposes concrete savings with figures.
scenarios.brief: Frau Albrecht from controlling wants to know why your team's cloud costs rose by 18 percent in the third quarter, to 42,300 euros a month. Explain the figures precisely, say how they are likely to develop, and propose savings. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Die Kosten sind gegenüber dem Vorquartal um 18 Prozent gestiegen.
words.en: Costs rose by 18 percent compared with the previous quarter.

words.de: Den größten Anteil hat mit gut 40 Prozent der Speicher.
words.en: Storage has the largest share, at a good 40 percent.

words.de: Das ist vor allem auf die neue Region zurückzuführen.
words.en: That's mainly due to the new region.

words.de: Je nachdem, wie stark die Daten wachsen, …
words.en: Depending on how fast the data grows, …

words.de: Vorausgesetzt, wir löschen alte Backups, sinken die Kosten deutlich.
words.en: Provided we delete old backups, costs will fall considerably.

words.de: mittels reservierter Kapazitäten
words.en: by means of reserved capacity

words.de: Das ließe sich bis Jahresende umsetzen.
words.en: That could be implemented by the end of the year.

words.de: Belastbare Zahlen liefere ich Ihnen bis Freitag.
words.en: I'll get you reliable figures by Friday.

student.title: Die Kostenrechnung vorstellen
student.setup: You are Frau Albrecht, head of purchasing at the engineering company where {{name}} is doing an internship. {{name}} has compared the costs of producing a plastic bracket by 3D printing and by milling: printing is cheaper up to about 350 pieces a year, because there are no tooling costs; above that, milling wins. You want to know which is cheaper at which quantity, how reliable the figures are and what {{he}} recommends. Ask precise follow-up questions ('Ist das eine Senkung um oder auf …?', 'Unter welcher Bedingung?'). Be friendly but exact; if a figure is vague, ask again. Use Sie.
student.goal: {{He}} presents the figures precisely (um / auf, von … auf, the share), makes the recommendation conditional with je nachdem, vorausgesetzt or es sei denn, and answers every follow-up with a figure.
student.brief: During your internship you compared the costs of 3D printing and milling a plastic bracket. Frau Albrecht, head of purchasing, wants to know which is cheaper at which quantity and how reliable your figures are. Present them precisely and make a recommendation. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Bis zu einer Stückzahl von etwa 350 ist der Druck günstiger.
words.en: Up to a quantity of about 350, printing is cheaper.

words.de: Darüber hinaus lohnt sich das Fräsen.
words.en: Beyond that, milling pays off.

words.de: Je nachdem, wie viele Teile wir pro Jahr brauchen, …
words.en: Depending on how many parts we need a year, …

words.de: Die Stückkosten sinken von 31 auf 18,40 Euro.
words.en: The unit cost falls from 31 to 18.40 euros.

words.de: Das entspricht einer Ersparnis von gut 40 Prozent.
words.en: That's a saving of a good 40 percent.

words.de: Vorausgesetzt, die Festigkeit reicht aus, …
words.en: Provided the strength is sufficient, …

units.title: Konflikte lösen
can_do: describe a conflict precisely: what it is about, what each side wants, and what really matters to them
concede a point and still hold my ground, in a dispute with a neighbour or in a mediation
lodge a reasoned Widerspruch against an official decision, on the phone and in writing
grammar: concession: wenngleich, so sehr … auch, mag … auch (So sehr ich Sie auch verstehe, …; Mag die Regel auch streng sein, sie gilt für alle)
zu …, als dass with Konjunktiv II (Es ist zu laut, als dass man schlafen könnte; …, als dass man es hätte sehen können)
Funktionsverbgefüge with passive meaning: zur Sprache kommen, in Kraft treten, zur Anwendung kommen, Berücksichtigung finden, zum Abschluss kommen
es geht um, es handelt sich um, es kommt darauf an (, ob / dass …): saying what a conflict is about
vocab_themes: neighbours and the house: die Hausordnung, die Nachtruhe, die Ruhestörung, hellhörig, Rücksicht nehmen auf, die Hausverwaltung einschalten
mediation: die Mediation, allparteilich, das Anliegen, das Bedürfnis, Positionen und Interessen, eine Einigung erzielen, aufeinander zugehen
the Widerspruch: der Bescheid, Widerspruch einlegen, die Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung, fristgerecht, die Begründung nachreichen, Akteneinsicht beantragen

scenarios.title: Ärger im Treppenhaus
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Hoffmann, 68, who lives in the flat below {{name}}'s. You meet {{him}} in the stairwell and you are annoyed: for weeks you have heard footsteps and loud talking after ten at night, and {{his}} bicycle stands in the stairwell, which the Hausordnung forbids. You threaten to keep a noise log and to involve the property management. You are upset but not unreasonable: calm down if {{name}} takes your point seriously and proposes something concrete, and then admit that you could have said something earlier. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} stays calm, concedes what is justified (so sehr … auch, wenngleich), explains {{his}} side, says what it is really about for {{him}} (Mir geht es um …), and agrees concrete steps with you.
scenarios.brief: In the stairwell you run into Frau Hoffmann, your downstairs neighbour. She is annoyed about noise after ten at night and about your bicycle in the stairwell, and is threatening to go to the property management. Calm things down, take her seriously and agree on something concrete. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Gut, dass Sie mich direkt ansprechen.
words.en: I'm glad you're speaking to me directly.

words.de: So sehr ich Sie auch verstehe, …
words.en: However well I understand you, …

words.de: Mir war nicht bewusst, dass man das bei Ihnen so deutlich hört.
words.en: I didn't realise you could hear it so clearly in your flat.

words.en: From now on, after ten I'll make calls in the living room.

words.en: From today I'll put the bike in the cellar.

words.en: What matters to me is a good relationship.

words.de: Bevor Sie die Hausverwaltung einschalten, sprechen Sie mich bitte an.
words.en: Before you bring in the property management, please talk to me.

scenarios.title: Vorgespräch zur Mediation
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Dr. Brandt, a mediator at the city's free community mediation service. Next week there will be a joint session between {{name}} and {{his}} neighbour Herr Wolf, who lives on the ground floor, wants barbecues on the balconies banned and has already complained twice to the property management about {{name}}'s barbecue, while {{name}} is annoyed about Herr Wolf's leaf blower early on Sunday mornings. Today you hold a one-to-one preliminary conversation with {{name}}. Ask what the dispute is about from {{his}} point of view, what really matters to {{him}} behind {{his}} position, what {{he}} could offer, and what a good outcome would be. Summarise now and then ('Ich höre heraus, dass …') and reframe accusations neutrally. Stay on both sides: never take sides against Herr Wolf. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains what the dispute is about with es geht um, es handelt sich um and es kommt darauf an, separates {{his}} position from {{his}} real interest, concedes a point with wenngleich or mag … auch, and names at least one concrete offer for the joint session.
scenarios.brief: A one-to-one conversation with Frau Dr Brandt, a mediator, before a joint session with your neighbour Herr Wolf. He wants barbecues on the balconies banned; you are annoyed by his leaf blower early on Sunday mornings. Explain what it is really about for you, and think about what you could offer. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Im Kern geht es um gegenseitige Rücksicht.
words.en: At its core, it's about mutual consideration.

words.de: Es handelt sich eigentlich um ein Missverständnis.
words.en: It's really a misunderstanding.

words.de: Mir geht es weniger um das Grillen als um den Ton.
words.en: For me it's less about the barbecue than about the tone.

words.de: Es kommt darauf an, ob er zu einem Kompromiss bereit ist.
words.en: It depends on whether he's willing to compromise.

words.de: Mag das Grillen auch erlaubt sein, …
words.en: Even if barbecuing is allowed, …

words.de: Wenngleich ich mich geärgert habe, …
words.en: Although I was annoyed, …

words.de: Ich könnte mir vorstellen, seltener zu grillen.
words.en: I could imagine barbecuing less often.

words.de: Das sollte im gemeinsamen Termin zur Sprache kommen.
words.en: That should be raised in the joint session.

scenarios.title: Der Abschleppbescheid
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Kraus, a case officer at the city's Ordnungsamt. {{name}} calls about a Kostenbescheid for 286 euros: {{his}} car was towed from a temporary no-parking zone that had been set up for a removal. At first you hold that the costs are justified ('Das Schild stand dort, das ist dokumentiert') and explain in slightly bureaucratic German that a Widerspruch must be lodged in writing within one month, as the Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung says ('Ihr Einwand wird selbstverständlich Berücksichtigung finden'). If {{name}} explains that the sign was put up less than a day before the towing, admit that the three-day lead time may not have been kept and that the case will be reviewed once the Widerspruch arrives. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains the facts precisely, argues with zu …, als dass and a concession (so sehr … auch), understands the formal steps (Frist, schriftlich, Begründung, Akteneinsicht), and announces a Widerspruch in correct formal language.
scenarios.brief: Your car was towed from a temporary no-parking zone that, as far as you know, was set up less than a day before. Now the Ordnungsamt wants 286 euros. Call Frau Kraus, the case officer, explain why you think the costs are not justified, and find out exactly how to lodge a Widerspruch. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Ich rufe wegen des Kostenbescheids vom 12. Mai an.
words.en: I'm calling about the notice of costs of 12 May.

words.de: Bei dem Halteverbot handelte es sich um ein mobiles Schild.
words.en: The no-parking zone was a temporary sign.

words.de: Das Schild stand zu kurz, als dass ich es hätte sehen können.
words.en: The sign was up too briefly for me to have seen it.

words.de: Soweit ich weiß, gilt eine Vorlaufzeit von drei Tagen.
words.en: As far as I know, a lead time of three days applies.

words.de: So sehr ich die Regel auch verstehe, …
words.en: However well I understand the rule, …

words.de: Ich werde fristgerecht Widerspruch einlegen.
words.en: I'll lodge an objection within the deadline.

words.de: Die Begründung reiche ich schriftlich nach.
words.en: I'll send the detailed reasons in writing later.

words.de: Ich beantrage Akteneinsicht, vor allem in die Fotos.
words.en: I'm requesting access to the file, especially the photos.

speaking.prompt: Two friends of yours share a flat and are fighting about cleaning and overnight guests. You have offered to mediate. In two minutes: say what the dispute is about for each of them, name the interest behind each position, grant each of them a point, and propose a solution they can both accept.
speaking.hint: Wenn ich dich richtig verstehe, geht es dir um … / Dir geht es eher darum, dass … / So sehr ich das auch verstehe, … / Mag das auch …, … / Es kommt jetzt darauf an, dass ihr …

writing.prompt: Write a formal Widerspruch against a Kostenbescheid (towing costs, or a fee you think is wrong): give the reference number, state the facts, argue with at least one concession and one zu …, als dass, ask for the decision to be revoked, and request access to the file.
writing.hint: Hiermit lege ich fristgerecht Widerspruch gegen … ein. / Bei … handelt es sich um … / … war zu …, als dass … / So sehr ich …, so wenig … / Ich bitte Sie, den Bescheid aufzuheben.

units.title: Vortrag und Referat
can_do: give a 15-minute talk at a conference or a company event in German: open it, guide the audience through it and close it, sounding like a speaker rather than someone reading a paper aloud
handle the question round: buy time politely, answer the actual question precisely, admit what I don't know and offer to follow up
turn a written text into a script for speaking: shorter sentences, clauses instead of noun chains, the heavy part after the verb
grammar: Ausklammerung and the Nachfeld in speech: comparisons, long prepositional phrases and afterthoughts after the final verb (Es hat länger gedauert als geplant; Ich habe angefangen mit einer ganz einfachen Frage)
signposting a talk: Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge; Wie eingangs erwähnt, …; Damit komme ich zum zweiten Punkt; Lassen Sie mich kurz zusammenfassen
cohesion across a talk with pronominal adverbs: darauf, davon, damit, darum (Darauf komme ich gleich noch zurück; Davon war vorhin schon die Rede; Genau darum geht es)
nominal style in speech: the noun on the slide, the clause in your mouth (Nach der Umstellung → Nachdem wir umgestellt hatten, …)
vocab_themes: the talk: der Vortrag, das Referat, die Folie, der Foliensatz, die Gliederung, der Einstieg, frei sprechen, vom Blatt ablesen, den Faden verlieren
guiding the audience: zunächst, anschließend, abschließend, im Folgenden, Wie Sie hier sehen, …, an dieser Stelle, kurz gesagt, Halten wir fest: …
the question round: die Fragerunde, die Rückfrage, Wenn ich Sie richtig verstehe, …, Da muss ich passen, Das reiche ich gerne nach, Habe ich Ihre Frage damit beantwortet?

scenarios.title: Der Konferenzvortrag
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Katrin Vogt, chair of a session at the 'Cloud-Native-Tage', a two-day German-language conference in Stuttgart. {{name}} gives a ten-minute talk about a project {{his}} team carried out: let {{him}} choose it, and if {{he}} hesitates, suggest how the team made its releases faster and safer. Introduce {{him}} in two sentences and give {{him}} the floor. While {{he}} talks, stay silent, except to say 'Noch zwei Minuten' once. Then run the question round, playing three listeners and naming each one first: Herr Albrecht asks a precise technical question; Frau Simsek asks a long, rambling question that is really two questions; Herr Kunz asks for something {{name}} cannot know (exact figures from another company, the cost of a tool). Thank {{him}} at the end. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} announces the structure at the start, signposts at least three transitions (Damit komme ich zu …, Wie eingangs erwähnt …, Darauf komme ich gleich zurück), speaks in clauses rather than noun chains, and handles all three questions: answers precisely, separates the double question, and admits honestly what {{he}} doesn't know and offers to follow up.
scenarios.brief: You're giving a ten-minute talk at a German-language conference in Stuttgart about a project your team carried out. The session chair, Dr. Vogt, introduces you; afterwards three people in the audience ask questions, one of them about something you can't know. Structure the talk clearly and handle the questions calmly. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge.
words.en: I'm going to talk about three things today.

words.de: Zunächst erzähle ich, wo wir angefangen haben.
words.en: First I'll tell you where we started.

words.de: Damit komme ich zum zweiten Punkt.
words.en: That brings me to my second point.

words.de: Darauf komme ich gleich noch zurück.
words.en: I'll come back to that in a moment.

words.de: Das hat länger gedauert als geplant.
words.en: That took longer than planned.

words.de: Wenn ich Sie richtig verstehe, sind das zwei Fragen.
words.en: If I understand you correctly, those are two questions.

words.de: Da muss ich leider passen.
words.en: I'm afraid I'll have to pass on that.

words.de: Die genauen Zahlen reiche ich gerne nach.
words.en: I'll gladly send you the exact figures later.

student.title: Das Referat im Seminar
student.setup: You are Prof. Dr. Andreas Brandt, who teaches the seminar 'Additive Fertigung' at a German Technische Universität. {{name}}, an exchange student, gives a ten-minute Referat on a topic of {{his}} choice from the field: if {{he}} hesitates, suggest why 3D-printed metal parts break differently from milled ones. Introduce the Referat in one sentence. While {{he}} talks, stay silent, except to say 'Noch zwei Minuten' once. Then run the discussion, naming each speaker first: you yourself ask a precise question about the method (Sie); the student Felix asks a long, rambling question that is really two questions; the student Mia asks for a figure {{name}} cannot know (the price of a metal printer, the results of another university). The students say du to {{name}}. Close with one sentence of friendly feedback.
student.goal: {{He}} announces the structure at the start, signposts at least three transitions (Damit komme ich zu …, Wie eingangs erwähnt …, Darauf komme ich gleich zurück), speaks in clauses rather than noun chains, and handles all three questions: answers precisely, separates the double question, and admits honestly what {{he}} doesn't know.
student.brief: You're giving a ten-minute Referat in the seminar 'Additive Fertigung' at a German university. Afterwards Professor Brandt and two fellow students ask questions, one of them about something you can't know. Structure the Referat clearly and handle the questions calmly. Sie with the professor, du with the students.

words.de: Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge.
words.en: I'm going to talk about three things today.

words.de: Zunächst erkläre ich kurz das Verfahren.
words.en: First I'll briefly explain the process.

words.de: Damit komme ich zu unseren Ergebnissen.
words.en: That brings me to our results.

words.de: Darauf komme ich gleich noch zurück.
words.en: I'll come back to that in a moment.

words.de: Wie ihr hier auf der Folie seht, …
words.en: As you can see here on the slide, …

words.de: Wenn ich dich richtig verstehe, sind das zwei Fragen.
words.en: If I understand you correctly, those are two questions.

words.de: Da muss ich leider passen.
words.en: I'm afraid I'll have to pass on that.

words.de: Das schaue ich nach und schicke es euch.
words.en: I'll look it up and send it to you all.

scenarios.title: Probelauf mit Feedback
scenarios.setup: You are Jana Becker, a colleague of {{name}}'s who has given many conference talks. {{name}} rehearses the first two minutes of a talk with you over video, and you give honest, friendly feedback the way a German colleague would: direct, but constructive. First ask what the talk is about and who the audience is. After the rehearsal, point out exactly two problems and quote {{him}}: for example a sentence full of nouns ('Nach erfolgter Einführung …'), a missing overview at the start, or a verb bracket so long that you lost the thread. Ask {{him}} to say those two passages again, better. React to what {{he}} actually says and praise what works. Finally ask how {{he}} would answer the question 'Und was hat das Ganze gekostet?' Use du.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains the talk's aim and audience, rehearses an opening with an overview, takes the feedback without defending every point, says two passages again for the ear (a clause instead of a noun chain, the heavy part after the verb), and answers the cost question or says how {{he}} will handle it.
scenarios.brief: Your colleague Jana has given lots of conference talks. You rehearse the first two minutes of yours with her over video; she'll tell you honestly what doesn't work and ask you to say it again, better. Take the feedback and improve on the spot. Informal: du.

words.de: Darf ich dir den Anfang einmal vortragen?
words.en: Can I run the opening past you once?

words.de: Der Vortrag richtet sich an Leute, die …
words.en: The talk is aimed at people who …

words.de: Wo hast du den Faden verloren?
words.en: Where did you lose the thread?

words.de: Ich sag's noch mal anders.
words.en: Let me say it differently.

words.de: Nachdem wir das umgestellt hatten, …
words.en: After we had switched that over, …

words.de: Guter Punkt, das ändere ich.
words.en: Good point, I'll change that.

words.de: Das würde den Rahmen sprengen.
words.en: That would go beyond the scope of the talk.

student.title: Probelauf mit einer Kommilitonin
student.setup: You are Jana Becker, a fellow student in {{name}}'s seminar who has given several Referate and works as a student assistant (Hiwi) at the institute. {{name}} rehearses the first two minutes of {{his}} Referat with you in a group room at the library, and you give honest, friendly feedback: direct, but constructive. First ask what the Referat is about and what the others in the seminar already know. After the rehearsal, point out exactly two problems and quote {{him}}: for example a sentence full of nouns ('Nach erfolgter Durchführung der Versuche …'), a missing overview at the start, or a verb bracket so long that you lost the thread. Ask {{him}} to say those two passages again, better. React to what {{he}} actually says and praise what works. Finally ask how {{he}} would answer the professor's question 'Und wie belastbar sind diese Ergebnisse?' Use du.
student.goal: {{He}} explains the Referat's aim and audience, rehearses an opening with an overview, takes the feedback without defending every point, says two passages again for the ear (a clause instead of a noun chain, the heavy part after the verb), and answers the professor's question or says how {{he}} will handle it.
student.brief: Jana, a fellow student in your seminar, has given several Referate. You rehearse the first two minutes of yours with her in a group room at the library; she'll tell you honestly what doesn't work and ask you to say it again, better. Take the feedback and improve on the spot. Informal: du.

words.de: Darf ich dir den Anfang einmal vortragen?
words.en: Can I run the opening past you once?

words.de: Die meisten im Seminar kennen das Verfahren noch nicht.
words.en: Most people in the seminar don't know the process yet.

words.de: Wo hast du den Faden verloren?
words.en: Where did you lose the thread?

words.de: Ich sag's noch mal anders.
words.en: Let me say it differently.

words.de: Nachdem wir die Proben gedruckt hatten, …
words.en: After we had printed the specimens, …

words.de: Guter Punkt, das ändere ich.
words.en: Good point, I'll change that.

words.de: Das würde den Rahmen sprengen.
words.en: That would go beyond the scope of the Referat.

scenarios.title: Ein Abend über Jordanien
scenarios.setup: You are Thomas Lindner, who organises the evening series 'Länder und Menschen' at the Stadtbibliothek in Freiburg. Tonight {{name}} gives a five-minute talk about Jordan to about thirty people, most of them retired people and students. Welcome the audience and introduce {{name}} in two sentences. Let {{him}} speak without interrupting. Then pass on questions from the audience, naming each person first: one about everyday life in Amman, one built on a stereotype ('Ist das Leben dort für Frauen nicht sehr schwierig?' or 'Ist das nicht gefährlich, so nah an den Krisengebieten?'), one about the water shortage, and one about what {{name}} would miss in Germany. React warmly and with curiosity. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} gives a structured five-minute talk with an opening that catches the audience's attention, a clear outline and a closing sentence, refers back to {{his}} own points (Wie eingangs erwähnt …, Davon habe ich vorhin schon gesprochen), and answers the stereotyped question with nuance instead of irritation.
scenarios.brief: The Stadtbibliothek in Freiburg runs an evening series about other countries, and tonight you're talking about Jordan for five minutes to about thirty people. Afterwards the organiser, Thomas Lindner, passes on questions from the audience, one of them based on a stereotype. Give them a picture of the real country. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Ich möchte Sie heute mitnehmen nach Amman.
words.en: Tonight I'd like to take you with me to Amman.

words.de: Wenn Sie an Jordanien denken, denken Sie wahrscheinlich an Petra.
words.en: When you think of Jordan, you probably think of Petra.

words.de: Zunächst ein paar Zahlen, dann der Alltag.
words.en: First a few figures, then everyday life.

words.de: Wie eingangs erwähnt, …
words.en: As I mentioned at the start, …

words.de: Davon habe ich vorhin schon kurz gesprochen.
words.en: I touched on that briefly earlier.

words.de: Das ist ein verbreitetes Bild, aber es stimmt nur zum Teil.
words.en: That's a common picture, but it's only partly true.

words.de: Wasser ist bei uns ein großes Thema.
words.en: Water is a big issue where I come from.

words.de: Damit bin ich am Ende. Vielen Dank fürs Zuhören.
words.en: That brings me to the end. Thank you for listening.

speaking.prompt: Give a five-minute talk about a project you were part of, for an audience that doesn't know it: open with a question or a surprising fact, announce your three parts, signpost every transition, describe one slide in words, and close with a one-sentence summary. Then answer the question 'Was würden Sie heute anders machen?'
speaking.hint: Wer von Ihnen hat schon einmal …? / Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge. / Damit komme ich zu … / Wie Sie hier sehen, … / Darauf komme ich gleich noch zurück. / Kurz gesagt: … / Heute würde ich …

student.prompt: Give a five-minute Referat about a project or a lab experiment from your studies, for fellow students who don't know it: open with a question or a surprising fact, announce your three parts, signpost every transition, describe one slide in words, and close with a one-sentence summary. Then answer the question 'Was würdest du heute anders machen?'
student.hint: Wer von euch hat schon einmal …? / Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge. / Damit komme ich zu … / Wie ihr hier seht, … / Darauf komme ich gleich noch zurück. / Kurz gesagt: … / Heute würde ich …

writing.prompt: Write the script for the first three minutes of a talk about a topic from your work: the greeting, an opening that catches attention, the outline and your first point. Write for the ear: short sentences, clauses rather than noun chains, comparisons and long additions after the verb, a signpost at every turn. End with two sentences you could say if someone asks you something you don't know.
writing.hint: Guten Morgen und vielen Dank für die Einladung. / Ich möchte mit einer Frage anfangen: … / Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge: zunächst …, dann …, und zum Schluss … / Damit komme ich zum ersten Punkt. / Da muss ich passen, aber ich reiche es gerne nach.

student.prompt: Write the script for the first three minutes of a Referat about a topic from your studies (a lab experiment, a design project, a material): the greeting, an opening that catches attention, the outline and your first point. Write for the ear: short sentences, clauses rather than noun chains, comparisons and long additions after the verb, a signpost at every turn. End with two sentences you could say if someone asks you something you don't know.
student.hint: Hallo zusammen, mein Referat heute geht um … / Ich möchte mit einer Frage anfangen: Wer von euch …? / Ich spreche heute über drei Dinge: zunächst …, dann …, und zum Schluss … / Damit komme ich zum ersten Punkt. / Da muss ich passen, aber ich schaue es nach.

student.title: Referat und Fachvortrag
can_do: give a 15-minute Referat in a German seminar: open it, guide the audience through it and close it, sounding like a speaker rather than someone reading a paper aloud
handle the questions from the professor and fellow students: buy time politely, answer the actual question precisely, admit what I don't know and offer to follow up
turn a written text into a script for speaking: shorter sentences, clauses instead of noun chains, the heavy part after the verb

units.title: Debatte
can_do: take part in a heated debate, on a panel or among friends, about the ethics of AI: state a position, concede what is true in the other side's argument and refute the rest
argue hypothetically: lay out what would happen if …, and test an argument against its consequences
hold my own in German Streitkultur: hard on the issue, soft on the person, keeping the floor when interrupted and ending on good terms
grammar: contrast connectors: zwar … aber, allerdings, hingegen, demgegenüber, während (KI spart zwar Zeit, aber …; Die einen sehen Chancen, die anderen hingegen Risiken)
concede and refute: Es mag sein, dass …, doch …; Ich gebe zu, dass …; Natürlich …, aber …; Der Einwand ist berechtigt, trotzdem …
Konjunktiv II for hypothetical argument: Was wäre, wenn …?; Angenommen, …; Das hätte zur Folge, dass …; Wäre das Verfahren transparent, könnte man …
modal verb substitutes: gezwungen sein, imstande / in der Lage sein, es ist erforderlich, haben zu, sein zu (Wir sind gezwungen, das zu klären; Das ist nicht zu verantworten)
vocab_themes: AI and ethics: die künstliche Intelligenz (KI), der Algorithmus, die Verantwortung, die Haftung, nachvollziehbar, die Diskriminierung, benachteiligen, der Datenschutz, regulieren
debating: die These, das Argument, der Einwand, einen Einwand erheben, ein Argument entkräften, widerlegen, einräumen, Das sehe ich anders, Das greift zu kurz
Streitkultur and the talk show: die Streitkultur, die Diskussionsrunde, jemandem das Wort erteilen, unterbrechen, Lassen Sie mich bitte ausreden, sachlich bleiben, zuspitzen

scenarios.title: In der Talkshow
scenarios.setup: You are two people on a TV discussion programme; start each turn with the speaker's name. Sandra Wolf is the host of 'Klartext'; today's question is 'Darf KI über Menschen entscheiden?', about software that pre-sorts job applications, grants loans or suggests diagnoses. Prof. Dr. Herbert Maier, an economist, is firmly in favour: machines are faster and fairer than prejudiced humans. {{name}} is the second guest, introduced as someone who uses AI every day and has lived in two cultures; let {{him}} choose a critical or a differentiated position. Sandra gives the floor, keeps answers short and pushes with pointed questions ('Ist das nicht ein bisschen naiv?'). Maier concedes good points ('Da haben Sie nicht ganz unrecht, aber …') and interrupts {{name}} once, mid-sentence; if {{he}} holds the floor politely, Maier lets {{him}} finish. Sandra closes by asking each guest for one final sentence. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} states a clear position, concedes at least one of Maier's points before refuting it (Es mag sein, dass …, doch …; zwar … aber), argues hypothetically at least once (Was wäre, wenn …? Das hätte zur Folge, dass …), holds the floor when interrupted, and ends with a one-sentence conclusion.
scenarios.brief: You're a guest on the TV discussion show 'Klartext'. The question: should AI decide about people, for example sort job applications or grant loans? The other guest, an economist, is firmly in favour and will interrupt you once. Take a clear position, concede what's true, refute the rest, and keep the floor. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Es mag sein, dass Maschinen schneller sind, doch …
words.en: Machines may well be faster, but …

words.de: Das ist zwar richtig, aber es greift zu kurz.
words.en: That's true, but it falls short.

words.de: Was wäre, wenn die Software sich irren würde?
words.en: What if the software got it wrong?

words.de: Das hätte zur Folge, dass niemand mehr haftet.
words.en: The consequence would be that nobody is liable any more.

words.de: Lassen Sie mich bitte ausreden.
words.en: Please let me finish.

words.de: Eine Software hingegen kann ihre Entscheidung nicht begründen.
words.en: Software, on the other hand, can't justify its decision.

words.de: Es ist erforderlich, dass ein Mensch das letzte Wort hat.
words.en: It is necessary for a human to have the last word.

words.de: Mein Fazit in einem Satz: …
words.en: My conclusion in one sentence: …

scenarios.title: Streit am Küchentisch
scenarios.setup: You are Rainer Kolb, 64, a retired master car mechanic from near Stuttgart and the uncle of a German friend of {{name}}'s. At a family birthday the conversation turns to a speed limit on the Autobahn, and you are firmly against one: 'Freie Fahrt für freie Bürger', German cars are built for it, the effect on the climate is tiny, and you have driven for forty years without an accident. You argue with gusto and a little exaggeration, but you are good-natured and never personal. Concede a point when it is a good one ('Gut, das lass ich gelten'), then come back with a new argument. If {{name}} gets personal or stays vague, say so. At the end, raise your glass and say you agree to disagree. Start with Sie and offer du after a few turns.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} disagrees firmly but stays sachlich, concedes at least one point and then refutes it (zwar … aber; Ich gebe zu, dass …, nur …), uses contrast connectors (hingegen, allerdings), argues hypothetically (Wenn es ein Tempolimit gäbe, …), and ends the argument on good terms.
scenarios.brief: At a family birthday, your German friend's uncle Rainer starts on his favourite topic: no speed limit on the Autobahn, ever. He argues loudly but good-naturedly. Disagree with him, concede what's fair, and keep it friendly. Formal at first; he'll offer du.

words.de: Da muss ich Ihnen widersprechen.
words.en: I have to disagree with you there.

words.de: Ich gebe zu, dass deutsche Autos sehr sicher sind.
words.en: I admit that German cars are very safe.

words.de: Nur: Darum geht es gar nicht.
words.en: But that's not the point at all.

words.de: Wenn es ein Tempolimit gäbe, würde es weniger schwere Unfälle geben.
words.en: If there were a speed limit, there would be fewer serious accidents.

words.de: In fast allen anderen Ländern hingegen ist das ganz normal.
words.en: In almost every other country, on the other hand, it's completely normal.

words.de: Das eine hat mit dem anderen nichts zu tun.
words.en: The one has nothing to do with the other.

words.de: Da werden wir uns wohl nicht einig.
words.en: I don't think we'll agree on that.

words.de: Darauf stoßen wir an.
words.en: Let's drink to that.

scenarios.title: KI im Team: ja oder nein?
scenarios.setup: You are two colleagues of {{name}}'s in a team meeting over video; start each turn with the speaker's name. The team has to decide whether developers may use AI coding assistants for production code. Petra Lang, the team lead, chairs neutrally and wants a decision with clear rules by the end. Stefan Hahn, a senior developer, is strongly against: AI-generated code is insecure, nobody knows the licences of the training data, juniors stop learning, and Stefan once saw an assistant invent a library that doesn't exist. Stefan argues hard but fairly and concedes points with 'Gut, das mag sein, aber …'. Petra asks {{name}} for {{his}} position first, and at the end asks {{him}} to sum up the agreed rules. Use du.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} takes a differentiated position, concedes at least two of Stefan's points and refutes or limits them, proposes concrete rules (a review for every suggestion, no customer data in prompts, a trial period) with modal verb substitutes (Es ist erforderlich, …; Wir wären gezwungen, …), and sums up the decision in a few sentences.
scenarios.brief: Your team is deciding whether developers may use AI coding assistants for production code. Stefan, a senior developer, is strongly against; Petra, your team lead, wants clear rules by the end of the meeting. Argue for a sensible position, take Stefan's objections seriously, and help the team agree. Informal: du.

words.de: Ich sehe das differenzierter.

words.en: You're right as far as the licences are concerned.
