student.title: KI in der Abschlussarbeit
student.setup: You are two people at a discussion evening of the Fachschaft Maschinenbau, the student council of {{name}}'s department; start each turn with the speaker's name. The question: may students use AI tools for their Bachelor's and Master's theses, and under what rules? Dr. Petra Lang, who supervises theses at the institute, chairs neutrally and wants concrete proposals to take to the examination board. Stefan Hahn, a Master's student, is strongly against: AI text is often wrong, it invents sources, nobody can tell who wrote what, and students stop learning to write. Stefan argues hard but fairly and concedes points with 'Gut, das mag sein, aber …'. Petra asks {{name}} for {{his}} position first, and at the end asks {{him}} to sum up the proposed rules. Stefan uses du; Dr. Lang uses Sie.
student.goal: {{He}} takes a differentiated position, concedes at least two of Stefan's points and refutes or limits them, proposes concrete rules (declaring every use, checking every source, doing the analysis of one's own data oneself) with modal verb substitutes (Es ist erforderlich, …; Man wäre gezwungen, …), and sums up the proposals in a few sentences.
student.brief: At a discussion evening of the student council, the question is whether students may use AI tools for their theses. Stefan, a Master's student, is strongly against; Dr. Lang, who supervises theses, wants concrete rules she can take to the examination board. Argue for a sensible position, take Stefan's objections seriously, and help the room agree. Du with Stefan, Sie with Dr. Lang.

words.de: Ich sehe das differenzierter.

speaking.prompt: Take a position on the question 'Sollte KI über Bewerbungen entscheiden dürfen?' and argue it for two minutes: your thesis, two arguments, the strongest counterargument, which you concede in part and then refute, one hypothetical consequence, and a one-sentence conclusion.

writing.prompt: Write a reader's letter to a newspaper that has published a commentary in favour of letting software pre-sort job applications. Say which article you are answering, state your position, concede one point of the commentary and refute it, argue with one hypothetical consequence, and end with a demand. Use zwar … aber, hingegen or allerdings, and at least one modal verb substitute.
writing.hint: Sehr geehrte Redaktion, zu Ihrem Kommentar „…“ vom … möchte ich Folgendes anmerken: / Der Autor hat zwar recht, wenn er schreibt, dass …, aber … / Wäre das Verfahren …, könnte man … / Es ist daher erforderlich, dass …

units.title: Literatur und Film
can_do: read a contemporary German novel or story and follow its narrative tenses, the characters' inner voices and its literary style
talk about a book or a film: setting, characters, perspective, what works and what doesn't, and recommend it or not
write a review (Rezension) of a book or a film for a blog or a magazine
grammar: literary Präteritum and Plusquamperfekt: narrating in the past and stepping further back (Sie trat ans Fenster. Er hatte den Brief nie abgeschickt.)
the old strong Konjunktiv II forms: käme, gäbe, wüsste, ginge, ließe, stünde, hülfe (Wenn ich es wüsste, …; als käme gleich jemand)
erlebte Rede: a character's thoughts in the third person and the narrative tense (Morgen würde sie es ihm sagen. War das wirklich alles gewesen?)
participial constructions in literature: Am Fenster stehend, …; Von der Reise erschöpft, …; Den Brief in der Hand, …
vocab_themes: reading a novel: der Roman, die Erzählung, der Erzähler, die Figur, die Handlung, der Schauplatz, die Rückblende, spielen in, handeln von, aus der Sicht von
the film: die Verfilmung, die Regie, die Besetzung, die Hauptrolle, das Drehbuch, die Kameraführung, der Spannungsbogen, synchronisiert, OmU
the review: die Rezension, gelungen, überzeugen, berühren, fesseln, sich ziehen, vorhersehbar, vielschichtig, empfehlenswert, Mein Fazit: …

scenarios.title: Im Lesekreis
scenarios.setup: You are Ingrid Hoffmann, 58, who runs a monthly book club (Lesekreis) at the Stadtbibliothek. Tonight there are five members, and you also speak for two of them, naming them first: Peter, who only reads crime novels, and Selin, a student who loves poetry. It is {{name}}'s turn to present a book {{he}} loves, from any literature (an Arabic novel in translation is very welcome). Ask what the book is about without giving away the end, who tells the story, what makes the style special, and why the club should read it. Peter is sceptical ('Passiert da auch was?'); Selin asks about the language and the translation. At the end the club votes on whether to read it next month. Use du; everyone in the club does.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} presents the book: setting, main character, narrator and plot without spoilers; describes its style with literary vocabulary (Figur, Erzähler, Rückblende, vielschichtig), answers Peter's scepticism, and makes a convincing recommendation.
scenarios.brief: It's your turn at the monthly book club in the town library: present a book you love, from any literature, and convince the others to read it next month. Ingrid runs the evening; Peter only reads crime novels and Selin loves poetry. Tell them what it's about without giving the end away. Informal: du.

words.de: Der Roman spielt in Kairo, kurz nach dem Krieg.
words.en: The novel is set in Cairo, shortly after the war.

words.de: Erzählt wird aus der Sicht einer jungen Frau.
words.en: It's told from the perspective of a young woman.

words.de: Es geht um eine Familie, die …
words.en: It's about a family who …

words.en: I won't give away any more.

words.de: Die Sprache ist schlicht, aber sehr genau.
words.en: The language is simple, but very precise.

words.de: Die Figuren wirken unglaublich glaubwürdig.
words.en: The characters are incredibly believable.

words.de: Es passiert nicht viel, aber man kann es kaum aus der Hand legen.
words.en: Not much happens, but you can hardly put it down.

words.de: Ich habe es in einem Zug gelesen.
words.en: I read it in one go.

scenarios.title: Nach dem Kino
scenarios.setup: You are Lukas, a German friend of {{name}}'s. You have just come out of the cinema together. Let {{name}} name the film if {{he}} wants to; otherwise it was 'Der Brief', the (invented) adaptation of a novel about a woman who returns to the flat of a mother who has died and leaves the mother's last letter unopened, shown in a small cinema. You loved it: you find the slow pace and the faces brilliant. Ask {{name}} how {{he}} liked it, disagree with anything negative, but give way to good arguments. Ask about specific things: the lead actress, the camera, the flashbacks, the ending, and whether the book is better. Suggest a drink and keep talking. Use du.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} gives a differentiated opinion with film vocabulary (Regie, Besetzung, Kameraführung, Spannungsbogen), backs it up with concrete scenes, concedes one of Lukas's points, and says whether {{he}} would recommend the film and to whom.
scenarios.brief: You've just come out of the cinema with your German friend Lukas. He loved the film; you're not so sure. Talk it over on the way to a bar: the actors, the camera, the ending, and whether the book was better. Informal: du.

words.de: Ehrlich gesagt hat mich der Film nicht ganz überzeugt.
words.en: To be honest, the film didn't quite win me over.

words.de: Die Hauptdarstellerin war großartig.
words.en: The lead actress was superb.

words.de: Die Kameraführung fand ich sehr gelungen.
words.en: I thought the camerawork was excellent.

words.de: In der Mitte hat er sich ziemlich gezogen.
words.en: It dragged quite a bit in the middle.

words.de: Das Ende war mir zu vorhersehbar.
words.en: The ending was too predictable for me.

words.de: Da gebe ich dir recht, aber …
words.en: I'll give you that, but …

words.en: The book is miles better.

words.de: Ich würde ihn allen empfehlen, die Geduld haben.
words.en: I'd recommend it to anyone with patience.

scenarios.title: In der Buchhandlung
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Albrecht, a bookseller in a small independent bookshop in Münster who loves recommending books. {{name}} wants a German-language novel, either for {{himself}} or as a present; ask which, then ask about taste: what {{he}} has liked so far, long or short, contemporary or classic, and how comfortable {{he}} is reading German. Suggest two or three real, well-known German-language novels, describing each briefly and accurately without spoilers; if you are unsure of a detail, say you would have to check. React to what {{he}} says, and if {{he}} mentions a classic such as Kafka or Fontane, comment on how the language reads today. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} describes {{his}} taste precisely (Ich lese gern Romane, die …; Mich interessieren vor allem …), asks about plot, style and difficulty, understands the bookseller's descriptions, and chooses a book for a reason.
scenarios.brief: You're in a small bookshop in Münster looking for a German novel, for yourself or as a present. The bookseller, Frau Albrecht, loves recommending books but needs to know your taste. Describe what you like and leave with a book you've chosen for a reason. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Ich suche einen deutschsprachigen Roman.
words.en: I'm looking for a German-language novel.

words.de: Er sollte nicht allzu lang sein.

words.de: Mich interessieren vor allem Geschichten über Familien.

speaking.prompt: Tell someone about a book or a film that has stayed with you: what it is about (without the ending), who tells it or from whose perspective, one scene you remember, what makes it good or not, and who you would recommend it to. Tell your scene in the Präteritum, as a narrator would.

writing.prompt: Write a review (Rezension) of a book or a film for a blog: a short introduction (title, author or director, genre), the plot up to the turning point, what works and what doesn't with concrete examples, and a Fazit. Use at least one participial construction and one 'als + Konjunktiv II'.
writing.hint: „…“ von … ist ein Roman über … / Erzählt wird … / Die Figuren wirken … / Besonders gelungen ist … / Allerdings zieht sich … / Man liest es, als wäre … / Mein Fazit: …

units.title: Geschichte und Erinnerung
can_do: follow a documentary, a museum text or a newspaper feature on German history: the division and 1989, the Gastarbeiter, the Nazi past and how it is remembered
talk with an eyewitness about their life story, asking good questions and reacting with tact
compare how Germany and my own country remember their past, and give my own view of it
grammar: Vorgangs- and Zustandspassiv in historical texts: Die Mauer ist 1961 gebaut worden; Am Morgen des 13. August war die Grenze abgeriegelt
kaum dass and ehe: Kaum dass die Grenze offen war, strömten Tausende nach Westberlin; Ehe jemand reagieren konnte, …
the future in the past: sollte + infinitive and würde (Er sollte seine Heimat nie wiedersehen; Damals ahnte niemand, dass sie bleiben würden)
genitive chains in historical writing: das Ende der Teilung des Landes; ein Kapitel der Geschichte der Bundesrepublik
vocab_themes: 1989 and reunification: die Teilung, die Mauer, der Mauerfall, die friedliche Revolution, die Montagsdemonstration, die Wende, die Wiedervereinigung, die DDR, die Stasi
the Gastarbeiter: das Anwerbeabkommen, die Anwerbung, der Gastarbeiter, der Anwerbestopp, der Familiennachzug, die erste Generation, die Vertragsarbeiter
remembrance: die Erinnerungskultur, das Gedenken, die Gedenkstätte, das Mahnmal, der Stolperstein, die Aufarbeitung, der Zeitzeuge, Das darf sich nie wiederholen

scenarios.title: Die Zeitzeugin
scenarios.setup: You are Renate Fischer, 71, who grew up in East Berlin and worked there as a nurse. You volunteer at an eyewitness café (Zeitzeugencafé) run by a museum in Berlin, where visitors can talk to people who lived through the GDR and 1989. {{name}} sits down at your table. Tell your story in pieces, only as {{he}} asks: your childhood behind the Wall, a brother who fled to the West in 1984, the great demonstration on Alexanderplatz on 4 November 1989, the night of 9 November at the Bornholmer Straße, and the years after reunification, when your hospital was closed and you lost your job. Your feelings are mixed: freedom, but also loss ('Nicht alles war schlecht, aber vieles'). React warmly to tactful questions and a little coolly to clichés ('War das nicht schrecklich?'). At the end, ask {{name}} how {{his}} own country remembers its history. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} asks open, tactful questions, follows up on details, reacts with empathy (Das kann ich mir kaum vorstellen; Wie ging es danach weiter?), retells one part of the witness's story in historical narrative (Kaum dass …, Sie ahnten nicht, dass … würde), and compares with how {{his}} own country remembers.
scenarios.brief: At an eyewitness café in a Berlin museum, you're sitting with Renate Fischer, 71, who grew up in East Berlin and lived through the night the Wall opened. She'll tell you her story piece by piece, if you ask the right questions. Listen, follow up, be tactful. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Darf ich fragen, wie Sie den neunten November erlebt haben?
words.en: May I ask how you experienced the ninth of November?

words.de: Wie war es, hinter der Mauer aufzuwachsen?
words.en: What was it like growing up behind the Wall?

words.de: Das kann ich mir kaum vorstellen.
words.en: I can hardly imagine that.

words.de: Wie ging es danach weiter?
words.en: What happened after that?

words.de: Haben Sie damals geahnt, dass es die DDR bald nicht mehr geben würde?
words.en: Did you suspect then that the GDR would soon no longer exist?

words.de: Was vermissen Sie, und was überhaupt nicht?
words.en: What do you miss, and what not at all?

words.de: Bei uns wird über die Vergangenheit ganz anders gesprochen.
words.en: Where I come from, people talk about the past very differently.

words.de: Vielen Dank, dass Sie das mit mir geteilt haben.
words.en: Thank you very much for sharing that with me.

scenarios.title: Die erste Generation
scenarios.setup: You are Mehmet Yıldız, 84, the grandfather of a German friend of {{name}}'s. You came from a village near Kayseri in 1964 to work in a car factory in Cologne, planning to stay two years. At a family dinner {{name}} sits next to you. You speak good, slightly old-fashioned German with the odd Turkish word. Tell your story only as {{he}} asks: the medical examination in Istanbul, the long train journey, the hostel with six men to a room, the shifts, learning German from the men on the assembly line, bringing your wife over in 1972, the plan to go back that never happened, and what Heimat means to you now (you joke that you are a guest who stayed sixty years). You are proud and humorous, not bitter, but you mention one hurtful experience. Ask {{name}} whether {{he}} would stay for good if {{he}} moved to Germany. Use Sie at first; offer du later.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} asks about Mehmet's life in order, reacts with interest and tact, uses historical narrative forms when asking or retelling (Kaum dass Sie angekommen waren, …; Damals wussten Sie noch nicht, dass Sie bleiben würden), and answers Mehmet's question about staying with a reasoned view.
scenarios.brief: At a family dinner you sit next to your German friend's grandfather, Mehmet, who came from Turkey in 1964 to work in a car factory in Cologne, planning to stay two years. Ask him about his life, from his arrival to today, and be ready for his question to you. Formal at first; he may offer du.

words.de: Wie war das, als Sie 1964 angekommen sind?
words.en: What was it like when you arrived in 1964?

words.de: Wo waren Sie damals untergebracht?
words.en: Where were you housed back then?

words.de: Haben Sie damals gedacht, dass Sie für immer bleiben würden?
words.en: Did you think back then that you would stay for good?

words.de: Wann haben Sie Ihre Frau nachgeholt?
words.en: When did you bring your wife over?

words.de: Aus zwei Jahren wurden sechzig.
words.en: Two years turned into sixty.

words.de: Wie haben Sie Deutsch gelernt?
words.en: How did you learn German?

words.de: Fühlen Sie sich hier zu Hause?
words.en: Do you feel at home here?

words.de: Das ist eine Geschichte, die man aufschreiben sollte.
words.en: That's a story somebody should write down.

scenarios.title: Ein Stolperstein vor der Tür
scenarios.setup: You are Clara Neumann, 35, a neighbour of {{name}}'s in Hamburg and a volunteer in the local Stolperstein initiative. You meet {{name}} on the pavement in front of your building, where you are polishing two brass Stolpersteine for Martha and Siegfried Cohn (an invented couple: a tailor and a seamstress, married, who lived in this house and were deported in 1941; their daughter escaped to England in 1939). {{name}} asks what you are doing. Explain what Stolpersteine are, what is known about the Cohns, and why your initiative researches the biographies in archives. Ask {{name}} what {{he}} thinks of this kind of remembrance and how history is remembered in {{his}} country. If {{he}} raises a critical point (for example, that people walk over the names), take it seriously: some critics say exactly that. Use du; you are neighbours.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} asks about the Stolpersteine and the family, understands the historical account (Vorgangs- and Zustandspassiv, sollte …), expresses respect and a considered opinion, and compares German remembrance with {{his}} own country's.
scenarios.brief: You meet your neighbour Clara on the pavement outside your building in Hamburg. She is polishing two small brass plates set into the pavement: Stolpersteine for a Jewish couple who lived in your house and were deported in 1941. Ask her about them, and share your view on how a country should remember. Informal: du.

words.de: Was machst du da eigentlich?
words.en: What are you doing there, actually?

words.de: Wer hat hier früher gewohnt?
words.en: Who used to live here?

words.de: Wann wurden sie deportiert?
words.en: When were they deported?

words.de: Weiß man, was aus der Tochter geworden ist?
words.en: Does anyone know what became of the daughter?

words.de: Ich bin schon so oft daran vorbeigegangen.
words.en: I've walked past them so many times.

words.de: Diese Art des Gedenkens berührt mich sehr.
words.en: This way of remembering moves me a lot.

words.de: Bei uns erinnert man sich ganz anders an die Vergangenheit.
words.en: Where I come from, the past is remembered very differently.

words.de: Darf ich beim nächsten Mal mithelfen?
words.en: Can I help next time?

speaking.prompt: Tell the story of an event in your country's or your family's history the way a short documentary would: what happened and in what order, what people didn't know then that we know now, and how it is remembered today. Then say in two sentences how this compares with remembrance in Germany.
speaking.hint: Im Jahr … wurde … / Kaum dass …, … / Damals ahnte niemand, dass … würde. / Er sollte … nie wieder … / Heute erinnert … an … / Anders als in Deutschland …

writing.prompt: Write a short portrait for a local newspaper of a person whose life was shaped by history: a grandparent, a neighbour, someone from the Gastarbeiter generation or from 1989, real or invented. Use the Vorgangs- and the Zustandspassiv, at least one 'kaum dass' or 'ehe', one 'sollte' for the future in the past, and one genitive chain.
writing.hint: Als … im Jahr … nach … kam, … / Untergebracht war … in … / Kaum dass …, … / … sollte … erst … wiedersehen. / Die Geschichte der … / Heute …

units.title: Verhandeln auf hohem Niveau
can_do: negotiate a contract with a client: scope, price and term, making conditional offers and saying no without damaging the relationship
handle crisis communication: explain an incident to an angry client, take responsibility without promising more than I can, and agree on next steps
sound firm and polite at once, with the diplomatic Konjunktiv, indirect phrasing and the right word order in the middle field
grammar: the diplomatic Konjunktiv: Wir wären bereit, …; Könnten Sie sich vorstellen, …?; Das müssten wir intern noch klären; Ich hätte da einen Vorschlag
indirectness: soft form, clear content (Das liegt etwas über unserem Budget; Das ist für uns schwer darstellbar; Der Termin erscheint uns sehr ambitioniert)
prepositional correlates: darauf bestehen, dass …; davon ausgehen, dass …; damit rechnen, dass …; Wert darauf legen, dass …
the middle field in detail: pronouns first (Ich schicke es Ihnen), dative before accusative with nouns, and where nicht goes (Wir können das Angebot so nicht annehmen)
vocab_themes: the negotiation: das Angebot, das Gegenangebot, der Spielraum, die Bedingung, das Zugeständnis, jemandem entgegenkommen, sich einigen auf, der Kompromiss, die Schmerzgrenze
contracts and money: der Vertrag, die Laufzeit, verlängern, der Festpreis, nach Aufwand abrechnen, der Tagessatz, der Rabatt, die Vertragsstrafe, die Kündigungsfrist
crisis communication: der Vorfall, der Ausfall, die Ursache, Wir bedauern den Vorfall sehr, Verantwortung übernehmen, nach jetzigem Stand, die Sofortmaßnahme, das Vertrauen zurückgewinnen

scenarios.title: Die Vertragsverlängerung
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Claudia Wagner, head of purchasing at a mid-sized logistics company in Hamburg and a long-standing client of {{name}}'s company, which runs and supports your cloud platform. The contract ends in three months. {{name}}'s company wants a price increase of eight per cent; you want no increase and, on top of that, support around the clock. You are friendly, experienced and tough: you never name your bottom line, react coolly to blunt demands and more warmly to conditional offers in Konjunktiv II ('Wenn Sie …, wären wir bereit …'). Make concessions only in return for something (a longer term, a later start for the increase). Insist on a guaranteed response time with a contractual penalty. Close by summarising what has been agreed and what is still open. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} opens with appreciation for the relationship, justifies the increase, makes conditional offers in Konjunktiv II, says no indirectly but clearly (Das ist für uns schwer darstellbar), uses prepositional correlates (Wir gehen davon aus, dass …; Wir legen Wert darauf, dass …), and agrees on a summary with next steps.
scenarios.brief: You're negotiating the renewal of a contract with Dr. Wagner, head of purchasing at a long-standing client. Your company wants an eight per cent price increase; she wants no increase and round-the-clock support on top. Find a deal both sides can live with, without giving anything away for free. Formal: Sie.

words.de: Wir schätzen die Zusammenarbeit mit Ihnen sehr.
words.en: We really value working with you.

words.de: Unsere Kosten sind deutlich gestiegen.
words.en: Our costs have risen considerably.

words.de: Wenn Sie den Vertrag verlängern würden, wären wir bereit, …
words.en: If you extended the contract, we would be prepared to …

words.de: Das ist für uns schwer darstellbar.
words.en: That's hard for us to do.

words.de: Wir gehen davon aus, dass …
words.en: We're assuming that …

words.de: Darüber können wir reden, unter einer Bedingung: …
words.en: We can talk about that, on one condition: …

words.de: Das müsste ich intern noch abstimmen.
words.en: I'd still have to clear that internally.

words.de: Lassen Sie uns festhalten, worauf wir uns geeinigt haben.
words.en: Let's put on record what we've agreed.

student.title: Der Praktikumsvertrag
student.setup: You are Jens Krämer from the HR department of a mid-sized company near Stuttgart that builds special machines. After a successful interview you call {{name}}, an engineering student from Jordan, to offer {{him}} an internship in the design department: five months from April, 900 euros a month. You can go up to 1,100 euros if {{he}} stays six months, and you can move the start to March; you cannot promise a thesis topic now, but you can agree to discuss one during the internship. Be friendly but careful with money ('Unser Spielraum ist begrenzt'), respond better to well-argued, conditional requests than to demands, and never volunteer a concession. Ask whether {{he}} needs a visa or other documents. Close by summarising the agreement and saying you will send the contract. Use Sie.

scenarios.title: Nach dem Ausfall
scenarios.setup: You are Thomas Berger, head of IT at an online pharmacy and a client of {{name}}'s company, which runs your shop's cloud platform. Yesterday the shop was down for four hours during a sales campaign, and you estimate you lost about 60,000 euros in orders. You call {{name}}, angry and under pressure from your own management. Start sharply ('Was war da gestern los?'). You want to know what happened, why nobody informed you during the first hour, whether it can happen again, and what {{his}} company will do to make up for it (you hint at the contractual penalty). Calm down step by step if {{he}} acknowledges the problem, gives facts without speculating, takes responsibility for what really was {{his}} company's fault and proposes concrete measures. Get angry again at excuses or blame-shifting. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} acknowledges the damage and apologises sincerely, separates what is known from what isn't (nach jetzigem Stand), explains the cause and the immediate measures, takes responsibility without promising more than {{he}} can, handles compensation diplomatically (Das müsste ich intern klären; Wir wären bereit, …), and agrees on a written follow-up.

scenarios.title: Der Gebrauchtwagen
scenarios.setup: You are Horst Wegener, 67, a private seller in a suburb of Hanover. If {{name}} points out real issues (the tyres will need replacing soon, a scratch on the rear door, the next TÜV inspection is due in two months), give way gradually; ignore vague complaints. Reject a lowball offer firmly but kindly. You would like cash and want to sell this week. Use Sie.

student.title: Verhandeln: Praktikum und Krise
can_do: negotiate an internship contract: duration, start date, pay and a thesis option, making conditional proposals and saying no without damaging the relationship
handle a crisis: explain to a sponsor or partner what went wrong, take responsibility without promising more than I can, and agree on next steps
sound firm and polite at once, with the diplomatic Konjunktiv, indirect phrasing and the right word order in the middle field
vocab_themes: the negotiation: das Angebot, das Gegenangebot, der Spielraum, die Bedingung, das Zugeständnis, jemandem entgegenkommen, sich einigen auf, der Kompromiss, die Schmerzgrenze
the internship contract: der Praktikumsvertrag, das Pflichtpraktikum, die Vergütung, die Laufzeit, die Probezeit, der Urlaubsanspruch, der Mindestlohn, die Abschlussarbeit im Unternehmen
crisis communication: der Vorfall, der Schaden, die Ursache, Wir bedauern den Vorfall sehr, Verantwortung übernehmen, nach jetzigem Stand, die Sofortmaßnahme, das Vertrauen zurückgewinnen

units.title: Redewendungen
can_do: understand the idioms and proverbs Germans use every day, in conversation, in the media and at work, including the ones whose image gives nothing away
use a handful of idioms naturally and correctly, with their fixed articles, prepositions and verbs, and quote a proverb by halves
judge when an idiom fits and when it is too casual, too much or a calque from Arabic or English, and say it plainly instead
grammar: idioms are frozen: the article, the preposition and the case never change (auf dem Holzweg sein, nicht alle Tassen im Schrank haben, ins Fettnäpfchen treten, jemandem reinen Wein einschenken)

the verb moves, the image stays: idioms in the Perfekt, in subordinate clauses, with modal verbs and with negation (Da hast du den Nagel auf den Kopf getroffen; …, weil er alles auf die lange Bank schiebt; keine Katze im Sack)
proverbs, and quoting them by halves (Wer A sagt, …; Der Apfel fällt nicht weit vom Stamm; Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund; Ende gut, alles gut)
when an idiom is too much: the wrong register, stacking, mixed images (Das schlägt dem Fass die Krone ins Gesicht) and calques from English or Arabic (nicht meine Tasse Tee, Auf meinem Kopf!)
vocab_themes: idioms of body and animals: die Nase voll haben, Hals über Kopf, Schwein haben, die Katze im Sack kaufen, den Kopf in den Sand stecken, jemanden auf den Arm nehmen
idioms for plans and effort: auf der Kippe stehen, ins kalte Wasser springen, Nägel mit Köpfen machen, am Ball bleiben, unter Dach und Fach sein, über den Berg sein
collocations and intensifiers: Kritik üben, Bilanz ziehen, eine Rolle spielen, in Kauf nehmen, stockdunkel, todmüde, heilfroh

scenarios.title: Jacke wie Hose

Speak naturally and fast, but if {{name}} asks what an idiom means, explain it with a short example. When {{he}} uses an idiom, react to it; if a piece is wrong (an article, a noun, a calque from English or Arabic), say with a grin what Germans actually say. Halfway through, ask {{him}} for an Arabic idiom, what it means literally and what the German equivalent would be. Use du.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} follows the idioms, asks about at least one (Was meinst du mit …?), uses at least three idioms correctly in context, and explains one Arabic or English idiom with its literal meaning and its closest German equivalent.

units.title: Register wechseln
can_do: turn an official letter in Amtsdeutsch into plain German for someone who has to act on it, and write a formal request in the register an office expects
understand and use the grammar of spoken German (weil with verb second, ellipsis, tun with an infinitive, the fronted topic) and know where each is out of place
follow casual and youth speech, including its Arabic and Turkish words, and answer in a register that fits the person in front of me
grammar: Amtsdeutsch into plain German and back: nouns into verbs, passive into who-does-what, noun-verb pairs into simple verbs (Die Antragstellung hat bis zum 30. Juni zu erfolgen → Stellen Sie den Antrag bis zum 30. Juni)
the long nested participial attribute of official texts, unpacked into a relative clause (die von Ihnen fristgerecht eingereichten Unterlagen → die Unterlagen, die Sie rechtzeitig eingereicht haben)

spoken grammar: weil and obwohl with verb second, ellipsis, tun + infinitive, the fronted topic picked up by der/die/das (…, weil ich hab keine Zeit; Schon erledigt; Verstehen tu ich das schon; Der Chef, der ist heute nicht da)
street grammar (Kiezdeutsch): dropped articles and prepositions (Ich geh Kino), lassma, verb third (Morgen ich geh Arbeit), and the standard German it maps to
vocab_themes: Amtsdeutsch and its plain twins: fristgerecht → rechtzeitig, unverzüglich → sofort, beifügen → mitschicken, in Kenntnis setzen → Bescheid sagen, das Nichtvorliegen, der Wohnungsgeber
the small words of speech: halt, eben, quasi, irgendwie, sozusagen, na ja, ne?, gell?, sag mal, oder so, passt schon
casual and youth words: krass, wild, Digga, lost, cringe, Aura, chillen, abgehen, wallah, yalla, der Ehrenmann

November vorzulegen.' 'Die Vorsprache hat persönlich unter Vorlage eines gültigen Reisepasses zu erfolgen.' 'Bei Nichtvorlage der angeforderten Nachweise kann der Antrag nicht bearbeitet werden.' 'Die von Ihrem Arbeitgeber auszufüllende Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis ist beigefügt.' After each sentence, ask what it means and what you have to do. If {{name}} answers in Amtsdeutsch, say you still don't understand. At the end, ask {{him}} to sum up your three to-dos. You speak German together because your children told you to practise. Use du.

scenarios.title: Ganz offiziell
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Schubert, a clerk at the Bürgeramt, on the phone. {{name}} calls because {{he}} cannot hand in a document by the deadline (the landlord's confirmation for the residence registration is due on Friday, and the landlord is abroad for three weeks). Speak correct, rather stiff Amtsdeutsch: 'Die Frist ist grundsätzlich einzuhalten', 'Eine Verlängerung ist nur in begründeten Ausnahmefällen möglich', 'die von Ihnen nachzureichende Bestätigung'. Ask for the Aktenzeichen, the reason, and whether {{he}} can prove it. If {{he}} speaks too casually (weil + verb second, 'halt', 'Digga'), stay polite but become noticeably cooler. If {{he}} makes a clear, formal request with a reason, grant two extra weeks and say {{he}} will receive it in writing. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} understands the clerk's Amtsdeutsch, keeps a formal register throughout (Sie, full sentences, no spoken grammar), gives the Aktenzeichen and a reason, asks formally for an extension (Ich möchte um eine Verlängerung der Frist bitten) and confirms the new date.
scenarios.brief: You are calling the Bürgeramt: your landlord's confirmation for your registration is due on Friday, but the landlord is abroad for three weeks. The clerk, Herr Schubert, speaks stiff official German. Stay just as formal and get an extension. Formal: Sie.

units.title: Deutschland, Österreich, Schweiz
can_do: understand Austrian and Swiss standard German in the shop, the newspaper and the house rules, and know which words and forms differ from German German
recognise the southern Perfekt (ich bin gestanden) and the regional greetings, and respond to them naturally
follow the gist of Bavarian, Austrian and Swiss German dialect, ask politely for standard German, and explain diglossia by comparing it with Arabic
grammar: Austrian standard German: its own words (der Jänner, heuer, der Paradeiser, der Topfen, das Sackerl, die Matura, der Sessel), genders (das Cola, das E-Mail) and forms (auf Urlaub, der Schweinsbraten, die Zugsverspätung)
Swiss standard German: no ß (die Strasse), its own words (das Velo, das Trottoir, das Billett, parkieren, zügeln, innert), genders (das Tram, der Match) and es hat for es gibt
the southern Perfekt: stehen, sitzen, liegen with sein (ich bin gestanden, ich bin gesessen, es ist gelegen), and the Perfekt for almost every past (ich bin gewesen)
understanding dialect: Bavarian and Austrian (i hob, des is net, a bissl), Swiss German (i ha, chunnsch), Swabian and Berlin markers, and diglossia: Mundart spoken, standard German written
vocab_themes: food across the borders: der Erdapfel, der Paradeiser, die Marille, der Topfen, das Schlagobers, die Semmel, der Karfiol, das Faschierte; das Poulet, die Glace, das Rüebli, die Peperoni
everyday life across the borders: die Matura, das Spital, der Gehsteig, die Stiege, der Kasten, das Sackerl, die Trafik; das Velo, das Trottoir, das Billett, der Perron, zügeln, der Abwart
greetings and goodbyes: Grüß Gott, Servus, Baba, Pfiat di, grüezi, grüessech, hoi, sali, merci vielmal, uf Widerluege, Moin, Mahlzeit

scenarios.title: Eine Melange, bitte
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Franz, a waiter in a traditional Viennese coffee house, about 60, charming in the slightly grumpy Viennese way. Speak Austrian standard German and use Austrian words naturally: Melange, Verlängerter, kleiner Brauner, Topfenstrudel, Marillenknödel, Schlagobers, Semmel, Paradeiser, Jause, Sackerl, heuer, Jänner. Address {{name}} with old-fashioned Viennese courtesy suited to {{him}} ('der Herr' or 'die gnädige Frau'). Mention in passing that the Marillenknödel are off the menu until summer and that the coffee house has been there since 1893. If {{he}} asks what a word means, explain it with pleasure and a little pride. When {{he}} asks for the bill, say 'Gerne, das macht vierzehn Euro achtzig' and wait to see whether {{he}} rounds up. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} orders using at least three Austrian words, asks about one unfamiliar term, understands Herr Franz's Austrian German, and pays with a small tip the Viennese way (Passt so / Stimmt so).
scenarios.brief: A traditional coffee house in Vienna. The waiter, Herr Franz, is charming in a slightly grumpy Viennese way and speaks Austrian German. Order a coffee and something to eat, ask about the words you don't know, and pay with a tip. Formal: Sie.

scenarios.title: Grüezi oder hoi?

Now and then drop a Swiss German word (Merci vielmal, Exgüsi, Ade, uf Widerluege); if {{name}} doesn't understand, repeat it in standard German, kindly. Ask where {{he}} has moved from and whether 'das Zügeln' went well. Use Sie.

scenarios.title: Auf der Hütte

units.title: Ironie und Zwischentöne
can_do: recognise irony, sarcasm and understatement in conversation, notes, emails and the media, from the particles and phrases that signal them
read what is meant but not said (a polite refusal, soft criticism, a brake in a meeting) and answer the real message or ask for it
use understatement, litotes and a rhetorical question myself, give irony back when it is friendly, and step out of it when I need a straight answer
grammar: irony signals: particles and set phrases that turn praise into criticism (Na toll. Das hat ja super geklappt. Sehr witzig. Schönen Dank auch. Das kann ja heiter werden.)
understatement and litotes: saying less to mean more (nicht ganz unproblematisch, nicht gerade billig, nicht ohne, kein Kinderspiel, ausbaufähig, Nicht schlecht!)
rhetorical questions with nicht, doch, etwa and schon (Ist das nicht schön? Habe ich es nicht gesagt? Hast du etwa …? Was soll man da schon machen?)
implicature: what polite German means but does not say (Ein interessanter Ansatz. Man könnte auch … Darüber können wir gern noch mal sprechen.), and how to ask for the plain message
vocab_themes: talking about tone: ironisch, sarkastisch, zynisch, der Unterton, die Anspielung, zwischen den Zeilen lesen, augenzwinkernd, trocken, eine spitze Bemerkung
soft criticism and polite refusal: ausbaufähig, Luft nach oben, nicht ganz glücklich, Ich sehe das etwas anders, Das müsste ich mir noch überlegen, mutig, Schauen wir mal
reacting to irony: Sehr witzig. Das war jetzt ironisch, oder? Spaß beiseite. Nimm's nicht persönlich. Wie meinst du das genau? Klartext, bitte.

scenarios.title: Ein interessanter Ansatz
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Ulrike Brandt, head of the platform department at {{name}}'s company, in a video call. {{name}} has sent you a written proposal to replace the company's commercial monitoring tool with an open-source stack. You are not convinced (the cost and risk of the migration, and whether the team has the skills), but you never say so directly. Use only indirect German: 'Ein interessanter Ansatz', 'Das ist durchaus mutig', 'Man könnte natürlich auch …', 'nicht ganz unproblematisch', 'Darüber sollten wir noch mal in Ruhe sprechen'. If {{name}} only thanks you and takes it as praise, end politely and vaguely. If {{he}} asks directly and politely what you really think, answer honestly, name your two concerns, and listen to {{his}} answer. Use Sie.

Do not say directly what bothers you unless {{name}} asks. If {{he}} answers with irony too, enjoy it and give some back; if {{he}} steps out of it and asks plainly, tell {{him}} plainly and agree on a simple rule together. Stay friendly underneath. Use du.

units.title: Sprachmittlung
can_do: convey a German letter, call or appointment to a family member in English or simple terms: what it says, what matters for them and what they have to do
convey an English or Arabic text, email or request into German for a German speaker, summarised for their purpose
interpret at an appointment, relaying questions and answers completely in both directions, checking what is unclear and explaining terms that have no equivalent
grammar: summarising for a purpose: the action and the deadline first, the rest marked as formality (Im Wesentlichen geht es darum, dass …; Für dich ist vor allem wichtig, dass …; Der Rest ist Formalität)

relaying speech: indirect questions with ob and question words, sollen for passed-on instructions, Konjunktiv I for formal relaying (Sie fragt, ob …; Er möchte wissen, wie lange …; Sie sollen …; Er sagt, er habe …)
terms without an equivalent: comparison and paraphrase (Das ist so etwas wie …; Das entspricht ungefähr …; Dafür gibt es kein deutsches Wort, gemeint ist …; Der Unterschied ist, dass …)

the interpreter's moves: third person, announcing, checking, asking for time and correcting (Ich übersetze kurz; Habe ich Sie richtig verstanden, dass …?; Einen Moment, ich frage nach; nicht …, sondern …)
vocab_themes: the official letter and its parts: das Schreiben, der Betreff, das Aktenzeichen, die Frist, der Bescheid, die Nachzahlung, die Vorauszahlung, nachreichen, Widerspruch einlegen, fällig
mediating and interpreting: übersetzen, dolmetschen, wörtlich, sinngemäß, zusammenfassen, auf den Punkt bringen, nachfragen, vermitteln
terms that need explaining: die Kaltmiete, die Warmmiete, die Nebenkostenabrechnung, die Überweisung, die Schufa, die Anmeldung, das Pfand; das Tawjihi, die Wasta, Vitamin B

scenarios.title: Ich übersetze für meine Mutter
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Sabine Kowalski, a family doctor (Hausärztin). {{name}}'s mother, who is visiting from Amman for three weeks and speaks Arabic and English but no German, has had a painful, swollen right knee for four days, and {{name}} interprets. Ask your questions in German one at a time: since when, whether there was a fall or a strain, other illnesses, regular medication, allergies. After each question that {{name}} relays, give the mother's answer yourself in English in square brackets, for example: [Mother, in English: 'Since Thursday. I didn't fall, but I walked a lot in the old town.'] {{name}} must relay it into German. Put one important detail into an answer that is easy to drop (the mother takes a blood thinner every day), and react to whether {{name}} passes it on. At the end, give your instructions in German (rest and cool the knee, no ibuprofen because of the blood thinner, a referral to an orthopaedic specialist if it is not better in five days) and ask {{name}} to sum them up before {{he}} explains them to {{his}} mother. units.title: Essay und Kommentar
can_do: write a newspaper-style commentary that takes a clear position and holds the reader to the last line
use rhetorical figures (anaphora, triad, antithesis, chiasmus, the rhetorical question) deliberately and sparingly
vary sentence openings and rhythm so a long German text reads easily, and hear the irony of a Glosse
grammar: figures of repetition: Anapher, Parallelismus and Trikolon (Wir brauchen mehr Busse, mehr Radwege, mehr Mut)
figures of contrast: the Antithese with nicht …, sondern, the Chiasmus, the rhetorical question (Wer will schon im Stau stehen?)
sentence rhythm: the short sentence after the long one, the verbless Ellipse, the colon and the dash
varied sentence openings: an object, an adverbial, a participle or a whole clause in the Vorfeld (Dieses Problem hat die Stadt lange ignoriert)
vocab_themes: text types and their parts: der Kommentar, die Glosse, der Essay, die These, der Einstieg, die Pointe, das Fazit
rhetorical figures by name: die Anapher, der Chiasmus, die Antithese, die rhetorische Frage, die Klimax, die Ellipse
the commentary voice: zugegeben, freilich, mitnichten, allenfalls, es greift zu kurz, unterm Strich

units.title: Fachdiskurs
can_do: read and explain a standard or specification (DIN, ISO), including exactly what its muss, sollte, darf and kann oblige me to do

give and answer peer review at expert level, and coin and decode specialist compounds

property words of technical German: -bar, -fähig, -frei, -arm, -beständig, -gerecht (wartungsarm, normgerecht, skalierbar)
the language of standards: muss / darf nicht, sollte, darf / braucht nicht, kann; ist … zu; es ist sicherzustellen, dass …
the expert's verdict on a scale of certainty: es steht fest, legt nahe, ist nicht auszuschließen; others' findings in Konjunktiv I

the expert report: das Gutachten, der Sachverständige, der Befund, die Bewertung, die Ursache, auf etwas zurückzuführen sein
peer review: die Begutachtung, die Einreichung, die Überarbeitung, nachvollziehbar, stichhaltig, der Einwand

units.title: Recht und Verwaltung
can_do: read a German statute: find the rule, its conditions and its exceptions, and follow citations like § 70 Abs. 1 Satz 1 VwGO
understand the parts of a Bescheid (Tenor, Begründung, Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) and what they mean for my rights and deadlines
lodge a reasoned Widerspruch within the deadline, in writing or in person, and explain it in formal and in plain German
grammar: the generalising relative clause of law: Wer …, wird …; Wer …, dem … (Wer die Frist versäumt, dem hilft kein Widerspruch mehr)
conditions and exceptions: sofern, soweit, es sei denn, sofern nicht, sofern nichts anderes bestimmt ist
reservations and references: unbeschadet and vorbehaltlich with the genitive, nach Maßgabe, gemäß; reading § 70 Abs. 1 Satz 1 i. V. m. …
obligation without modal verbs: ist … zu, hat … zu, bedarf + genitive, ist befugt; the Bescheid formula war … abzulehnen
vocab_themes: the statute: das Gesetz, der Paragraf, der Absatz, die Vorschrift, der Tatbestand, die Rechtsfolge, in Kraft treten
the Bescheid: der Tenor, die Begründung, die Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung, die Bekanntgabe, die Frist, das Aktenzeichen, bestandskräftig
the Widerspruch: Widerspruch einlegen, fristgerecht, die Begründung nachreichen, abhelfen, der Widerspruchsbescheid, der Einspruch

scenarios.title: Der Festsetzungsbescheid
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Petersen, an advisor at the Verbraucherzentrale. {{name}} brings a Festsetzungsbescheid from the regional public broadcaster: it sets arrears of the Rundfunkbeitrag plus a late-payment surcharge (Säumniszuschlag) for {{his}} flat. But {{name}} shares the flat with a flatmate who has paid the fee all along, and only one fee is due per flat. Ask {{him}} to read out the Tenor and the Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung, ask when the letter arrived, and explain the way forward: a Widerspruch within one month to the broadcaster named in the letter, quoting the flatmate's Beitragsnummer. Point out that the objection does not by itself stop the payment demand, and that a plain email is usually not enough. Use Sie; patient and clear.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} explains the Bescheid in {{his}} own words (what was decided, why, the deadline), understands why only one fee is due per flat, and dictates the core of a reasoned Widerspruch.
scenarios.brief: You've received a Festsetzungsbescheid for the broadcasting fee, with arrears and a late-payment surcharge, although your flatmate has paid the fee for your flat all along. An advisor at the Verbraucherzentrale helps you with the letter. Explain what it says, check the deadline with her, and work out together what your Widerspruch must say.

scenarios.title: Widerspruch zur Niederschrift
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Brandl, an official at a city's Bürger- und Ordnungsamt. {{name}} comes to your counter to lodge a Widerspruch zur Niederschrift (you write it down and {{he}} signs) against the refusal of a residents' parking permit: the car is registered to a family member who lives elsewhere, but {{name}} uses it every day. Ask for the Aktenzeichen, the date of the Bescheid and when it arrived, what exactly {{he}} objects to and why, and whether {{he}} can now hand in the keeper's declaration that {{he}} uses the car permanently. Read back one sentence in formal German and ask {{him}} to confirm or correct it. Explain what happens next: your office checks whether it can grant the objection (abhelfen); otherwise the next higher authority decides with a Widerspruchsbescheid. Formal, correct, a little bureaucratic. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} gives the reference data precisely, states what {{he}} objects to and why in formal German (die Voraussetzung ist erfüllt), corrects the record where needed, and understands the next steps.
scenarios.brief: Your application for a residents' parking permit was refused because the car isn't registered to you. You go to the office in person to lodge a Widerspruch 'zur Niederschrift': the official writes it down and you sign it. Give him the reference data, explain why the refusal is wrong, check what he writes, and find out what happens next.

scenarios.title: Was steht im Gesetz?
scenarios.setup: You are Lea, a friend of {{name}}'s in the sixth semester of law (Jura). {{name}} wants to move out of {{his}} rented flat and asks you about the notice period. Show {{him}} § 573c Abs. 1 Satz 1 BGB ('Die Kündigung ist spätestens am dritten Werktag eines Kalendermonats zum Ablauf des übernächsten Monats zulässig.') and ask {{him}} to put it into plain German, then to apply it: in November 2026 the third Werktag is Wednesday 4 November (Saturdays count as Werktage, Sundays and public holidays don't), so a letter that reaches the landlord on 3 November ends the tenancy on 31 January 2027, one that arrives on 5 November on 28 February 2027. Correct gently if {{he}} confuses sending and receipt (what counts is when the landlord receives it), and mention that a tenant's notice must be in writing and signed by hand (§ 568 BGB), so an email or a WhatsApp message is not enough. Use du; relaxed, a little proud of what you know.
scenarios.goal: {{He}} paraphrases the provision in plain German, applies it correctly to two dates, and knows the form requirement.
scenarios.brief: You want to move out of your rented flat, and a friend who studies law shows you the provision on notice periods in the Civil Code. Put it into plain German, then work out when your tenancy would end, depending on the day your letter arrives. Ask her about anything that's unclear.

units.title: Literatur in der Tiefe
can_do: read demanding literary prose and poetry, from Büchner and Heine to Kafka and contemporary writers, and say what a passage does as well as what it says
recognise archaic and literary forms (the dative -e, genitive objects, ward, poetic inversion) and know which of them still work today

grammar: archaic and literary forms: the dative -e (vom Lande, im Hause), verbs with a genitive object (gedenken, sich entsinnen), ward, dropped endings (Gebirg, hätt)
word order for emphasis: object, participle or predicate in the Vorfeld (Geschlafen hat er nicht), the split noun (Geld hat er keins), the poetic final verb (Ein Birnbaum in seinem Garten stand)
the absolute phrase and the participial opening of literary prose (Den Hut in der Hand, trat er ein; Kaum erwacht, …)
the Konjunktiv of narration: als + verb second (als hätte …), ohne dass … hätte, the wish (Wäre ich doch …), old strong forms (stünde, käme)
vocab_themes: talking about a text: der Erzähler, die Erzählperspektive, das lyrische Ich, die Parabel, das Motiv, die Deutung
the literary register: alsbald, unversehens, jäh, gewahr werden, gleichwohl, innehalten
the literary world: die Lesung, der Lesekreis, die Neuerscheinung, das Feuilleton, die Rezension, der Literaturpreis

scenarios.title: Im Lesekreis

Then offer a different interpretation (for example a religious one, or one about bureaucracy) and ask {{him}} to weigh it against {{his}} own. Quote a short line of the text now and then. scenarios.title: Bei der Einbürgerungsbehörde
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Schäfer, a caseworker at a city's naturalisation office (Einbürgerungsbehörde). {{name}} has applied for German citizenship after several years in Germany and comes for the appointment. Check the documents (passport, a language certificate of at least B1, the certificate for the 'Leben in Deutschland' test, proof that {{he}} supports {{himself}}). Ask why {{he}} wants to become German, and ask {{him}} to explain in {{his}} own words what the commitment to the freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung means (for example human dignity, free elections, the separation of powers, equal rights for women and men) and why Germany bears a special responsibility for its history. Finally explain the next step: the Einbürgerungsurkunde is handed over, often at a ceremony, together with a solemn declaration. Friendly, thorough, formal. Use Sie.
